A keyboard-driven, cascading command palette engine for TiddlyWiki. Open with a hotkey, type to filter, Right-arrow to drill into a stage, Space to open the action menu on any tiddler row, Esc to back out, Enter to fire an action. Extensible via declarative entry and action tiddlers — no widget code required.

## What it does

- **Cascading stages.** Picking an entity drills into a new stage scoped to that entity (its action menu, or a related set). Stages form a stack; breadcrumb shows the path; Esc pops one level at a time and closes at root.
- **Declarative protocol.** Adding a new cascade edge is one tiddler. Tag `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/{entry,action}`, set `ca-*` fields, save.
- **Generic engine.** Knows nothing about your data model. Catalogue plugins like `rimir/orga-palette` ship the entries/actions; the engine just walks them.
- **Filter substitution.** Filter expressions in entries and actions receive `<<query>>`, `<<picked>>`, `<<parent-picked>>` so cascades can chain naturally.

## Features

The engine ships well beyond the core cascade:

- **Views & channels** — compose the result list as Entries / All tiddlers / By namespace / By parent / Hybrid / By date, picked from a pill strip.
- **Axes** — per-channel grouping chains (year → month → day, status → prefix, etc.), editable live.
- **Filters, visibility & presets** — pill strips that narrow results, hide entries, and save/replay view + filter combinations.
- **Leaders** — single-key shortcuts (clear constraints, tree-picker, save preset, help, …).
- **Side-preview pane** — per-menu or tag-auto-attached wikitext preview of the focused row.
- **Row icons, lenses (name / icon / annotation row decorations, authored in-palette), sticky context, deep-tree search**, and a typed-field edit protocol (toggle / number / text / date settings, confirm gestures, reorder).

See the in-plugin documentation tab for the full protocol and authoring guide.

## Inspiration

Souk21's `souk21/commandpalette` showed how powerful a TiddlyWiki keyboard palette can be. This plugin is from-scratch because souk21's flat data model (one input, one list, terminal Enter) didn't fit the cascading shape we wanted — but the philosophy of "extend by tagging a tiddler" is the same.

|0.0.119 |2026-06-08 |''Channel/view "Overview" rows.'' A channel (`ca-channel-preview`) or view (`ca-view-preview`) can name a summary template; the root stage then emits a synthetic ''Overview'' row — a non-drill no-op leaf, search-skipped, pinned to the top of its group (`_buildOverviewRows` + a `_pinTop` pass in `_sortRowsForView`). Focusing the row renders the template in the side preview; ''Enter'' moves focus into the preview pane. To make this work, the side preview now surfaces a ''selected'' row's own `ca-preview-template` (`_selectedRowPreview`), not only a drilled one, and the auto-open fallback anchors on the template even when the row has no title (`_activePreviewContext`). Optional `-preview-name` / `-preview-title` set the row/pill label and the caption above the body. New fields appear both in the long-tail field editors (`cp-view-edit-rows` / `cp-channel-edit-rows`, ''preview'' group) AND as an always-visible ''summary'' pill on the Structure strip's view header + each explicit channel mini-row (↵ edits, DEL clears, ''—'' when unset) via a new `summary` case in `_pillEditDescriptor`. Tests: +new Jasmine specs (`test-overview-rows.js`, `test-side-preview-rows.js`) + summary-pill descriptor specs in `test-view-editor.js`. |
|0.0.118 |2026-06-05 |''VIEW → CHANNEL restructuring + lens inheritance + richer presets.'' The structure-layer vocabulary is renamed to ''CHANNEL'' throughout: a CHANNEL is a named, reusable group of palette rows a view composes by reference (`ca-view-channels`). The data model moves `ca-layer-*` → `ca-channel-*`, the tag to `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/channel`, and the shipped channels to the `channels/` namespace; the parser ''dual-reads'' the old fields so un-migrated user tiddlers keep working, and a one-time browser startup migration (`cp-channel-migration`) rewrites them in place (idempotent, user-only, write-on-change). ''Lens inheritance:'' a view declares a default decoration lens per slot (`ca-view-lens-name`/`-icon`/`-annotation`); each channel may override (`ca-channel-lens-*`) or inherit, and the view can LOCK a slot (`ca-view-locked`) to force its lens everywhere. Resolution is now channel-aware — the same tiddler can decorate differently in two channels — baked once per view-load (`_applyLensInheritance`) and keyed into the row-decoration cache by channel. The three standalone lens-chooser strips are ''relocated'' into the Structure strip's view→channel tree (a view-default chooser per slot in the view row + a per-channel override chooser in each channel row, with inherit/lock cues; `l` toggles a lock; new-lens creation moves to Manage lenses) — the old strip rendering, focus/Tab-cycle plumbing and strip-driven lens-edit flow (`_renderLensStrip` / `_handleKeydownLensSlot` / `_beginLensEdit` / `_commitLensEdit` etc.) are fully removed, and the shared dual-read helpers live in `cp-utils`. ''Presets'' now capture/restore all six transient subsystems — filters, visibility, reach, search-meta, search-field, and sticky-context (schema `v:2`); a v1 preset restores the new subsystems to empty (lenses are deliberately excluded — they travel with the view). Tests: +19 Jasmine specs (`test-lens-inheritance`, `test-lens-choosers`, `test-presets`) plus updated rename specs. |
|0.0.117 |2026-06-04 |''Large root-set perf warning (Phase 6).'' A view whose root set resolves to more rows than a configurable threshold (`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/large-root-set-warning`, default 2000; `0` disables) now emits a one-time `console.warn` — that full set is rebuilt and re-decorated on every keystroke, so it's the dominant per-keystroke cost. The warning fires once per view + stage-kind (not per keystroke) and re-arms when the set drops back below the threshold, suggesting a narrower `ca-view-roots` or a filter pill (`cp-stack`: `getLargeRootSetWarning` / `_maybeWarnLargeRootSet`, called from `recomputeStage`). Adjustable live via Settings → Large root-set warning. Tests: +10 Jasmine specs (`test-large-root-set.js`) and +2 Playwright specs (`cascade-palette-perf.spec.js`). |
|0.0.116 |2026-06-04 |''In-palette entry + action editors (Phase 5).'' Two new top-level entries — ''📋 Manage entries'' and ''⚡ Manage actions'' — make command entries and actions authorable without hand-editing tiddlers, completing the in-palette definition-editor arc (views / layers / axes / lenses / entries / actions). Each lists every definition with a ''+ New …'' creator (prompt a name → save a fresh tagged tiddler with sane defaults → reopen) and one drillable row per definition. Drilling opens a per-facet field editor (`cp-entry-edit-rows`: identity / kind / leaf-behaviour / drill-target; `cp-action-edit-rows`: identity / the three discovery facets entity-type·applies·action-when / behaviour), binding each field in place via `ca-bind-*`, with a confirm-gated delete. USER definitions edit in place; a SHIPPED (shadow-only) one is clone-protected (''Clone to a custom … to edit''). One generic lifecycle (`cp-def-editor`: new / clone / delete, spec-driven) and one generic list builder (`cp-def-rows`) serve both kinds; a shared `cp-row-builders` util supplies the text/toggle row shapes. Tests: +13 Jasmine specs (`test-def-editor.js`) and +3 Playwright specs (`cascade-palette-entries.spec.js`). |
|0.0.115 |2026-06-04 |''Long-tail view + layer field editors (Phase 4).'' The Structure strip edits a view's core structure (roots/children/leaf/label/axes) and enum facets (sort/include-entries/grouping) live; everything else is now editable from ''Manage views → Edit all fields…'' — a drill (`cp-view-edit-rows`) listing the exhaustive view-scoped long tail as `ca-bind-*` rows, grouped: ''identity'' (name/hint/icon/order), ''display'' (count-format + show-count / containers-first / show-action-preview / show-side-preview / context-aware yes-no toggles), ''sort detail'' (sort-field/sort-key), ''picking'' (pick-mode / pick-emits-filter / after-fire), and ''row defaults'' (row-hint/icon/order/next-scope/items-from — the per-row overrides not surfaced as pills). Each explicit structure-layer the view composes drills into its own editor (`cp-layer-edit-rows`: name, `ca-layer-source`, `ca-layer-include-position`, and the `ca-layer-row-*` defaults). USER views/layers edit in place; a SHIPPED (shadow-only) view offers fork-to-edit and a shipped layer a Structure-strip hint (editing in place would write an override). The drill targets the active view via a new `$:/state/…/active-view` mirror written by `_setActiveView`, self-healing to the default view. `ca-position-<view>` stays on the entry, not the view. Tests: +14 Jasmine specs (`test-view-edit-rows.js`) and +3 Playwright specs (`cascade-palette-view-fields.spec.js`, incl. a live toggle write + layer drill). |
|0.0.114 |2026-06-04 |''Fork view is now a deep clone (Phase 2 tail).'' ''Manage views → Fork current view'' (`_forkView`) previously copied only the view's `ca-view-*` fields and kept its layers/axes ''shared'' with the source — editing the fork's structure mutated the original. It now makes a fully independent persisted copy: every explicit structure-layer and grouping axis the view references is copied into a private title, with `ca-view-layers` / `ca-view-axes` / each forked layer's `ca-layer-axes` rewritten to the copies (new `_forkLayer` / `_forkAxis` / `_forkAxisChain`). Per-axis params are preserved (the chain re-serialises as JSON only when some entry carries params, else a plain title list); the built-in entries layer and any unresolvable reference pass through verbatim. Axis field-copy is shared with the axis editor (`cp-axis-editor`'s `_copyAxisFields`) and layer field-copy is factored into `_copyLayerFields` (also used by `_beginLayerEdit`) — no duplication. Tests: +10 Jasmine specs (`test-view-fork.js`: deep-copy, param preservation, entries/unresolvable passthrough, byte-level isolation, collision-safe titles) and +2 Playwright specs (`cascade-palette-fork.spec.js`: the real Manage-views → Fork loop on shipped ''Hybrid'' for layers and a seeded axis-bearing view for axes). |
|0.0.113 |2026-06-04 |''In-palette axis create / edit / delete (Phase 3).'' A new ''🧭 Manage axes'' entry (`entries/manage-axes.tid`) makes the axis mechanics editable, transparently via raw filters — mirroring ''Manage lenses''. (1) ''+ New axis…'' (`cp-axis-editor.js`) seeds a scratch axis and opens the raw `ca-axis-key` editor with a live ''✓ N matches'' count, then prompts a name and saves under `…/axes/`. (2) Each existing axis drills into a per-facet field editor (`cp-axis-edit-rows.js`): bind-edit name / hint / icon / order / key / label / sort / sort-keys / empty-label in place, with a read-only info row naming any `<axis-param-X>` placeholders (their values are set per use in a layer's chain), and a confirm-gated delete. (3) A shipped (shadow-only) axis is clone-protected — ''📋 Clone to a custom axis to edit'' (`_cloneAxisToUser`) copies it to `…/axes/` first. Created axes feed the existing Structure-strip chain picker. Tests: +14 Jasmine specs (`test-axis-edit-rows.js`, `test-axis-editor.js`) and a 5-spec Playwright suite (`cascade-palette-axes.spec.js`, incl. an end-to-end check that an axis chain buckets the tree). |
|0.0.112 |2026-06-04 |''Per-lens field editor + auto-resolve; test hardening.'' (1) ''Field editor'' — drilling a lens in ''Manage lenses'' now opens a per-facet editor (`widgets/cp-lens-edit-rows.js` / `cp-lens-rows.js` / `cp-lens-actions-rows.js`): bind-edit ''name / chip / when / order'' in place, toggle default slots, edit each slot's ''filter'' + ''template'', pick the actions mode, and confirm-delete — all via the standard declarative `ca-bind-*` rows (replaces the prior `EDIT_LENS_MESSAGE` single-filter edit). Shipped lenses are clone-protected (''📋 Clone to a custom lens to edit'' → `CLONE_LENS_MESSAGE`). (2) ''Auto-resolve (no silent override)'' — a slot renders its filter OR its template and the filter wins; each row now carries a `ca-on-commit` that clears its sibling on a non-blank commit (last-edited wins; blank-commit promotes the other), plus a conflict marker (''filter ● active'' / ''template ⚠ ignored'') for pre-existing both-set lenses. (3) ''Fix'' — removed the dead `"preview"` row from the keyboard dispatch table: the `_handleKeydownPreview` it pointed at was never actually defined (the 0.0.108 "wired up" was incomplete), so it was a no-op; preview stays a focus in the Tab cycle with native scroll + click-to-switch candidate pills. (4) ''Tests'' — +11 lens-adjacent Jasmine specs (4-path action union, default-slot re-seed, `_cloneLensToUser`, row-icon applies/payload) and a new Playwright E2E suite (lenses / lens-editor / nav / structure / extras) covering the browser-only rendering (annotation chip + rich template) unit tests can't reach. |
|0.0.111 |2026-06-04 |''Lenses — actions, templates + annotation, and a Manage-lenses list.'' (1) ''Actions via lens'' — `ca-lens-actions` lets a lens contribute actions: `via-entity-type` declares it owns the standard entity-type bridge (the kind lens), any other value is a filter returning action titles to surface on a row. Always-on — gated only by `ca-lens-when`, never by slot selection, so kind actions stay available with the Icon slot off. Unions into `loadActionsForType` as a fourth path. (2) ''Template projections + annotation slot'' — `ca-lens-<slot>-template` renders rich wikitext per visible row (output HTML cached per data-change; filter wins when both set); the ''annotation'' slot now renders as a trailing chip. Ships generic ''Modified'' (filter) + ''Tags'' (template) annotation lenses (off by default). (3) ''Manage lenses list'' — the entry now lists every lens (''↵'' edit · ''DEL'' delete a custom lens) alongside a ''+ New … lens…'' creator per slot (`widgets/cp-lens-rows.js`); ''↵'' on a row edits via the new `EDIT_LENS_MESSAGE`. |
|0.0.110 |2026-06-04 |''Lenses — unified row-decoration model.'' The former row-label (name) + structure-toggle (icon) subsystems are replaced by one ''lens'' (tag `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/lens`) projecting ''name'' / ''icon'' / ''annotation'' slots via `ca-lens-<slot>-filter`, gated by `ca-lens-when`, seeded by `ca-lens-default`. Each slot is its own single-select chooser strip below the view strip. ''In-palette authoring'' (new `cp-lens-editor.js`): the ''➕ New…'' slot pill / ''Manage lenses'' entry create a lens with a live-preview filter editor; ''e'' edits, ''DEL'' deletes (confirm). ''DEL on a view pill'' now deletes the view too (confirm; shipped views refuse). One merged per-row resolver + cross-render cache (`cp-row-decorations.js`, keyed by selection + change-count) so decorations persist across keystrokes. ''Fix:'' lenses no longer relabel palette command rows (entries-layer rows like "Find entity"). Removed `cp-row-label-pills.js` / `cp-structure-toggles.js`; a prior `…/row-label` pick resets once to the default name lens. |
|0.0.109 |2026-06-03 |''New extension point — structure toggles (tag `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/structure-toggle`): boolean on/off pills in the Structure strip's view header, flipped with Space/Enter. A toggle may carry `ca-struct-row-icon-filter` to supply a per-data-row leading icon while on (new `widgets/cp-structure-toggles.js`). Enables e.g. kind's "Kind icons" toggle.'' |
|0.0.108 |2026-06-03 |''Side-preview pane: ←/→ now cycle between candidate previews when two or more apply, applying each on landing (no Enter/Space). The handler and hint text already existed but `"preview"` was never registered in the keyboard dispatch table — now wired up; Esc-from-preview (return to input) also starts working as a side effect.'' |
|0.0.107 |2026-06-03 |''Single-select pill strips (view / preset / row-label) now apply on ←/→ landing — navigating onto a pill selects it, no Space/Enter needed. Space/Enter still work; preset's trailing "+" save pill stays an explicit gesture. Driven by a central `selectOnMove` descriptor flag in `_handleKeydownPillStrip`.'' |
|0.0.106 |2026-06-03 |''Shift-Tab now restores the focus you last held in the group you switch into (the menu row, the filter pill you were editing, …) instead of always snapping to input / the bottom-most pill; falls back to the old defaults when that slot has disappeared or was never visited.'' |
|0.0.105 |2026-06-02 |''Fixes: JSON sub-path commits now serialize compactly (prevents the `.tid`→`.json` file swap); doc-template integration repaired (correct `rdt.*` fields + page-template wrapping) so the documentation tab renders branded tabs; `ca-visibility-filter` now evaluated in widget scope; `getDefaultValue` uses the public shadow API; README refreshed.'' |
|0.0.104 |2026-06-02 |''Perf: smooth arrow-key navigation over the menu — holding ↑/↓ no longer hangs and jumps several rows at once.'' |
|0.0.103 |2026-06-02 |''Type-ahead from any section — a printable character pressed outside the input now jumps focus to the input and appends it (standard command-palette convention).'' |
|0.0.102 |2026-06-02 |''Fix: whole-field `application/x-string-array` writes now store a TW titlelist, not a JSON array literal (`widgets/cp-items.js`).'' |
|0.0.101 |2026-06-02 |''Row-label pills — single-select strip that overrides how each data row's display name is rendered (new widgets/cp-row-label-pills.js).'' |
|0.0.100 |2026-06-02 |''Side-preview pane auto-opens on tag-candidate match — no more per-menu / per-row opt-in required.'' |
|0.0.99 |2026-06-02 |''Header click restores focus to the popup's last logical section (widgets/cascade-palette-widget.js).'' |
|0.0.98 |2026-05-31 |''View-history back-stack — Esc out of an action/leader-initiated view jump returns to the previous view.'' |
|0.0.97 |2026-05-31 |''Sticky-context variables are now ambient in every filter eval routed through `_filterInScope` (cp-actions.js).'' |
|0.0.96 |2026-05-31 |''Bug fix — `ca-view-after-fire: stay` is now actually honored on fire (cp-firing.js).'' |
|0.0.95 |2026-05-31 |''Two UX polish changes: pin/unpin keep the palette open; Right-arrow on a tree-view leaf opens its action menu.'' |

! Components

* ''Widget'' (`widgets/cascade-palette-widget.js`) — implements the palette: stage stack, keyboard router, result rendering, action invocation.
* ''Startup module'' (`widgets/cascade-palette-startup.js`) — mounts the widget into `document.body` at boot via `<$cascade-palette/>`. Independent of any page template tag so the palette works in any UI mode (default wiki, appify, custom themes).
* ''Hotkey binding'' (`config/shortcut-binding.tid` + `config/shortcut-key.tid`) — standard TW keyboard shortcut machinery. Press the configured key (default Ctrl-Space) and TW dispatches the `rimir-cascade-palette-open` message that the widget catches via `$tw.rootWidget`.

! Stage stack

The palette is a stack of stages, growing on Right-arrow / Space / Enter-on-drill, shrinking on Esc / ArrowLeft. Stage shapes:

;`kind: "root"`
:The initial stage. Items come from tiddlers tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/entry`, sorted by `ca-order` then `ca-name`.
;`kind: "tree"`
:A tree-stage from a view's channel. Pushed when the user Right-arrows into a container (tree node with children). The parent path is carried in `parentPath`; child rows come from the originating channel's `ca-channel-children` filter (or the view's `ca-view-children` for implicit-channel views).
;`kind: "filter"`
:A stage scoped by a filter expression. Pushed when the user drills from a `ca-kind: drill` entry or action. Items are dynamic — tiddler titles (or bare strings) returned by `ca-next-scope`.
;`kind: "actions"`
:An action-menu stage. Pushed in three situations: (a) the user Right-arrows on a typed leaf — `ca-channel-row-entity-type` set on the emitting channel; (b) the user Spaces on any tiddler row whose discovery scan produced at least one applicable action; (c) the user drills on a dynamic entity item in a filter stage. Item-discovery unions three parallel paths, deduplicated by action title: ''catalogue'' — actions whose `ca-entity-type` matches the row's bound type (plus globals tagged `ca-entity-type: *`); ''configured-field auto-derive'' — when `$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/entity-type-field` is set to a field name (e.g. `rimir/kind` ships it as `kind.type`), an action's `ca-entity-type: <X>` ALSO matches any row whose tiddler carries `<configured-field>: <X>`; ''filter'' — actions whose `ca-applies` filter matches when `<currentTiddler>` is the row's title. All three paths are further narrowed by each action's optional `ca-action-when` applicability filter.
;`kind: "confirm"`
:A two-row Confirm / Cancel stage pushed when a leaf action carries `ca-confirm: yes`, or on Delete-on-row for destructive list operations. The consequence text shows inline as the Confirm row's hint AND in the detail drawer banner.

The keyboard router does one of:

* ''Type'' → update current stage's `query`, recompute items.
* ''Up/Down'' → move `selectedIndex` via `_moveMenuSelection` — a lightweight class-swap (move `rcp-row-selected` between two cached row `<li>`s, scroll into view, refresh hint) rather than a full `renderResults()`, so key auto-repeat stays smooth. The per-row side-preview refresh is debounced (`_scheduleRowChangePreview`, ~90ms) so the heavy preview/graph render fires only for the row the user settles on.
* ''Right-arrow'' → drill from the selected item (push new stage). On tree containers, descends children; on typed catalogue leaves, pushes the action-menu stage.
* ''Space'' → on toggle/text/number/date kinds, kind-specific edit; on any other tiddler row whose action-discovery scan produces at least one applicable action (catalogue or `ca-applies`-filter), pushes the action-menu stage. Empty match → silent no-op. Works in tree views (By namespace / By parent / Hybrid), not just the catalogue.
* ''Tab'' → cycle focus //between sections// (input → preset → filter → view → menu → details → …). Never drills. ''Shift-Tab'' jumps between the pill-group (top strips) and the main group (input/menu/details/preview).
* ''Enter'' → fire the selected item's default behaviour (leaf action OR push if drill).
* ''Esc'' → pop one stage. From input at root depth, closes the palette; from menu at root depth, refocuses input.
* ''Shift-Esc'' → close the palette from any focus and any depth in one keystroke. Freezes the current stack to `$:/temp/rimir/cascade-palette/saved-stack` so the next open resumes here.
* ''Type-ahead (Tier 4)'' → a printable character (single-char `key`, no Ctrl/Alt/Meta, not IME) pressed in any section //other// than the input, that the section handler did not consume, refocuses the input and appends the character. The dispatcher runs this last and gates on `e.defaultPrevented`, so every section-specific single-char gesture (Space-to-toggle, ±-on-number-rows, pill Space/Enter) wins first — they signal ownership by calling `preventDefault`. Lets you start typing to filter from anywhere, the standard command-palette convention.

! Axes — per-channel grouping chains

A channel can declare a chain of ''axes'' that group the channel's source set by a derived key — year, month, day, status, prefix, or any tiddler-to-string mapping you can write as a filter. Each axis runs at one tree depth: first axis at root, second under each first-axis bucket, and so on. Axes ''compose with the channel's recursive `children` filter'': past the chain, the children filter takes over with the source narrowed to whatever leaf bucket the user drilled into. The two concepts are orthogonal halves of the same descent — axes form the top, children forms the bottom.

!! The descent at a glance

```
depth:    0       1       2       3            4        5       …
        ┌─────────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────┐
data:   │  AXIS CHAIN (buckets)   │  │  RECURSIVE TREE         │
        │  parentPath[i] = key    │  │  parentPath[i] = tiddler│
        │  source = channel.roots,  │  │  filter = channel.children│
        │  narrowed by axis-keys  │  │  currentTiddler = parent│
        │  matching parentPath    │  │                         │
        └─────────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────┘
                       ↑                ↑
                    transition: parentPath.length === chain.length
```

`parentPath` (the array carried on every tree-stage) holds bucket keys for indices `0..chain.length - 1` and real tiddler titles for indices `chain.length..`. The reader doesn't need a type check: depth alone tells the engine which interpretation applies.

!! Three useful configurations of a single channel

|!Axes |!Children |!Behaviour |
|empty |empty |Flat list. `roots` is the source, every row is a leaf. (Today's ''All tiddlers''.) |
|empty |set |Pure recursive tree — same `children` filter at every depth, source narrowed by `<currentTiddler>` rebinding. (Today's ''By parent'', ''By namespace''.) Axes never engage. |
|set |empty |Pure grouping. Buckets all the way down; at the deepest axis, the leaves are tiddlers from the narrowed source — no further descent. (Shipped ''By date''.) |
|set |set |Bucket the source first, then descend each leaf-bucket tiddler via `children` as today. E.g. ''By parent, sliced by year'' — TOC tiddlers grouped by year, each TOC then expanding its tag-subtree. |

!! Transition mechanics

At the exact moment `parentPath.length === chain.length` (axes consumed but no tiddler drilled yet), the engine calls `cp-axes.sourceAfterAxes` to emit `channel.roots` narrowed by every parent bucket key. Each result row is a real tiddler — and runs through the same row-builder as every other tiddler row in the engine: `_isLeafInLayer` decides drill vs. leaf by asking ''"does `channel.children` return anything under this tiddler?"'' (empty children → always leaf; non-empty → `_treeContainer = true`).

That single test is the only place axes and children indirectly meet. After it, drilling appends the picked tiddler title to `parentPath`, depth becomes `chain.length + 1`, and the descent is in standard recursive mode — `channel.children` evaluates with `<currentTiddler> = parentPath[last]` exactly like today's tree views.

!! Two practical caveats

# ''`channel.roots` is doing double duty.'' It's both the ''universe to bucket'' (when the axis chain is evaluating) AND the ''forest roots'' at the transition. If you write `ca-channel-roots: [!is[system]]`, every non-system tiddler is bucketable AND every non-system tiddler is a recursive root candidate. If you write `ca-channel-roots: [tag[TOC]]`, only TOC-tagged tiddlers participate in either phase. Same filter, two consumers.
# ''Cross-bucket children.'' Past the transition, `channel.children` runs with `<currentTiddler>` = the parent ''tiddler'', not the bucket path. A 2025-tagged child of a 2026 TOC tiddler will appear in the 2026 subtree — the date stops following you down. That's almost always what you want for tag-trees. If you need date-coherent descent, intersect a date predicate into `ca-channel-children`.

!! Axis schema (tag `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/axis`)

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`ca-axis-name` |Pill label / picker label |
|`ca-axis-hint` |Detail-drawer help text |
|`ca-axis-key` |Filter (`<currentTiddler>` = row tiddler) returning the bucket key |
|`ca-axis-label` |Optional pretty-label filter (`<currentTiddler>` = bucket key) |
|`ca-axis-sort` |`first-seen` (default) / `asc` / `desc` / `enum` |
|`ca-axis-sort-keys` |Space-separated key order; used by `enum` sort |
|`ca-axis-empty-label` |Bucket label when the key resolves to empty (default `—`) |
|`ca-axis-icon` |Optional bucket glyph |

Parametric axes (e.g. shipped `by-field`) reference `<axis-param-X>` variables in their key/label filters; per-pill params are stored alongside the axis title in the session state and bound at evaluation time as `<<axis-param-X>>` widget variables.

!! Pill UX

The Structure pill-row (`viewconfig` strip) renders each axis in the active chain as a yellow ''by'' / ''→'' pill in that channel's mini-row, plus a dashed ''+'' pill at the end. In expanded mode (Tab to the strip, Enter to expand):

* ''Backspace / Delete'' on a focused axis pill removes it from the chain.
* ''Shift-← / Shift-→'' reorders it within the chain.
* ''Enter'' on a chain pill swaps it via the axis picker.
* ''Enter / Space'' on the ''+'' pill appends a new axis.

The picker is itself a cascade stage — a (`_freezeItems`) filter-stage listing every tiddler tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/axis`. On commit, `cp-axes.writeChainState` persists the new chain to `$:/state/rimir/cascade-palette/channel-axes/<channel-slug>` and `popStage` bounces focus back to the strip. Cancel (Esc) leaves state untouched.

!! State precedence

* Session override in `$:/state/rimir/cascade-palette/channel-axes/<slug>` wins over the channel's declared `ca-channel-axes`.
* Resetting (delete the state tiddler) reverts to the declared default.
* `$:/state/...` survives reload but is NOT filesystem-synced — same pattern as `cp-leader` state.

Schema in the state tiddler: JSON `{ "axes": [ { "title": "...", "params": {…} }, ... ] }`. Bare strings are accepted shorthand for un-parameterised axes in either the declared default OR the state — `parseChainSpec` handles both shapes.

!! Performance

Axis `keyFn` results are memoised per `(axisTitle + paramsHash) × tiddlerTitle`, invalidated on `wiki.getChangeCount()`. First touch of the cache fills it; subsequent re-renders cost O(rows visited at the current depth), not O(source). For a 3-axis chain over a 2500-tiddler source: ~150ms cold first-render, then near-zero on subsequent keystrokes.

The `groupBy` / `sortGroups` primitive is loaded from `$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/lib/grouped-tree.js` when the mindmap plugin is installed (soft-dep); a tiny inline fallback covers the case where mindmap isn't around — same algorithm, no feature degradation.

! Side-preview pane

Right-column wikitext renderer that opens when the user drills into a row carrying preview registration. Two parallel mechanisms feed candidates into the pane:

* ''Per-menu (explicit)'' — an entry/action declares ''`ca-preview-template`'' (+ optional ''`ca-preview-context`'' filter / ''`ca-preview-title`'' caption / ''`ca-preview-name`'' pill label / ''`ca-preview-per-row`'' flag). At drill-time, `_attachPreviewToStage` resolves the context filter in the parent stage's substitution scope and stamps the result onto the newly-built stage record.
* ''Tag-based (auto-attach)'' — any tiddler tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/side-preview`'' is a candidate the engine evaluates against the active context. Its ''`ca-preview-applies`'' filter is run with `<currentTiddler>` bound to the context — non-empty result = candidate applies. The tagged tiddler IS the template body by default (override via ''`ca-preview-template`''); other fields (''`ca-preview-name`'', ''`ca-preview-title`'', ''`ca-preview-order`'') tune the pill label, caption, and sort order. cp re-evaluates the applies filter on every render so per-row drills surface different previews per selected row.

''Activation'' — four entry conditions are recognised: (a) ''per-menu template'' set via `ca-preview-template`; (b) ''tag-only opt-in'' (the row sets `ca-preview-context` or `ca-preview-per-row` without a template — the pane activates and populates purely from tag candidates); (c) ''inheritance'' from a parent per-row stage — for inherited sub-stages of kind ''`actions`'' the context is locked to the drilled-into row (the entity), preventing action-menu navigation from re-anchoring the preview to action titles; for ''`filter`''/''`tree`'' sub-stages the per-row flag propagates so navigation inside still tracks sub-rows; (d) ''auto-open fallback'' — when no stage on the stack carries an explicit signal, `_activePreviewContext` falls back to the topmost stage whose active view doesn't carry ''`ca-view-show-side-preview: no`'' (default `yes`) AND which has a selected row with a non-empty title. The row title becomes the synthetic context; tag-based candidates attach via the normal applies-filter path. When no candidate matches, `_resolvePreviewCandidates` returns empty and the pane stays hidden — no placeholder UI. Sub-stages drilled from an auto-open parent stay locked to the entity via the stack walk: filter / action / confirm stages don't carry their own `viewTitle`, but the parent stage's `selectedIndex` hasn't moved since the drill, so the walk-up surfaces the locked-row entity correctly. ↑/↓ at an auto-open top stage re-render the pane via a new `_shouldRerenderPreviewOnRowChange()` helper (auto-open is inherently per-row by construction).

''Pill row'' — when ≥2 candidates apply, a horizontal pill row is rendered above the title strip. The active pill is highlighted; ←/→ when the preview pane has focus cycles forward/backward (wraps both ends); click switches directly. With a single candidate the row is suppressed via the `:empty` CSS selector — the pane looks identical to the single-candidate case. The user's choice is pinned by ''template title'' (stashed on the stage as `_previewActiveTemplate`) so candidate-list reshuffles (a per-row context change drops some candidates, or a higher-priority plugin's preview appears) re-find the same pill rather than snapping to index 0.

''Caching'' — the rendered widget tree is cached by `(depth, contextTitle, templateTitle)`. Selection-tracking re-renders inside the same preview reuse the DOM; switching pills re-renders (template changes); per-row context change re-renders. The wiki change hook dispatches `refresh(changes)` into the cached widget tree for non-invalidating changes (so form inputs inside the preview's template stay reactive without rebuild), and drops the cache entirely when either the active template tiddler, the context tiddler, OR any side-preview-tagged tiddler is created/modified/deleted.

! Row icons

A row-icon is a small glyph rendered in a footer strip below the main row line, surfacing affordances on the row's backing tiddler — opening an external URL, jumping to an attachment, etc. — without cluttering the name column. Lives in `widgets/cp-row-icons.js`; the strip renders only when at least one icon resolves so quiet rows look untouched.

''Registration'' — any tiddler tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/row-icon`'' is an icon candidate. The shipped ''`row-icons/url.tid`'' is the only one out of the box: it carries `ca-row-icon-key: url` (the built-in field-scanning resolver), `ca-row-icon-glyph: 🌐`, and `ca-row-icon-message: open-url`. Authors ship their own by declaring `ca-row-icon-applies` (filter that gates the icon — `<currentTiddler>` is the row's title) + either `ca-row-icon-action` (wikitext actions with `<<payload>>` bound to the resolved value) or `ca-row-icon-message` (built-in JS dispatch — currently only `open-url` is recognised).

''URL resolution'' — the `url` key is hard-coded in cp-row-icons.js's `_resolveUrlForTitle`. It reads ''`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/url-fields`'' (default `url`, space-separated for multiple), walks the configured fields on the row's tiddler in order, and returns the first value matching ''`/^(?:https?|ftp|ftps|mailto|tel):/i`''. Other URL prefixes (`magnet:`, `vscode:`, etc.) can be added by editing the regex; for now the strict allowlist keeps `tiddler-bearing` config text from leaking into the strip as an icon.

''Row eligibility'' — `computeRowIconsForItem` reads ''`item.rawTitle || item.title`'' and skips rows where neither resolves OR `item.isSynthetic` is set. That covers every kind that has a backing tiddler: ''entries'' (their own tiddler title), ''actions'' (same), ''tree-view rows'' across every view (the row's source tiddler — entries view, By Namespace, By Parent, By Date, Hybrid channels, etc.), and ''dynamic filter-stage items'' (`evaluateFilterStage` stamps both `title` and `rawTitle`). Excluded: synthetic JSON-array rows (`ca-items-from`), confirm-stage Confirm/Cancel placeholders, axis-picker rows that wrap an axis tiddler with no domain field. The same regex / filter then runs against the row's tiddler — typically the user's `url` field on a real tiddler — and surfaces the icon when matched.

''Resolution per render'' — `_appendResultRow` calls `_renderRowIcons(rowEl, item)` after match snippets but before the row's mousedown handler. The helper invokes `computeRowIconsForItem(item)`, stamps `item._rowIcons` with the live list, and appends `<div class="rcp-row-icons">` only when at least one icon survived. The Alt-↵ keyboard branch reads `item._rowIcons` directly — no recomputation. The footer hint reads the same `_rowIcons` field per-row via the menu-hint builder (see ''Footer hint'' below) to surface the Alt-↵ / Ctrl-Alt-↵ gestures when they actually fire on the selected row.

''Caching'' — `_loadRowIcons` caches the icon registry by `wiki.getChangeCount()`. The change-hook (cascade-palette-widget.js) drops the cache when any row-icon-tagged tiddler is created/modified/deleted ''OR'' when the URL_FIELDS_CONFIG tiddler changes. Per-item icon resolution is NOT cached — it runs every render — but the per-icon JS path is a tiny field read on the row's tiddler, so 30 rows × 1 icon ≈ 30 cheap lookups per keystroke. Generic filter-based icons cost one `wiki.filterTiddlers` per row per icon; ship a `ca-row-icon-applies` that returns fast (e.g. `[<currentTiddler>has[some-field]]`) rather than a full graph walk.

''Firing'' — `fireRowIcon(item, icon, e, mode)` is the single dispatch point. `mode` is `"primary"` (default, bound to Alt-↵ and glyph click) or `"alt"` (bound to Ctrl-Alt-↵). In `primary` mode it reads `icon.message` / `icon.action`; in `alt` mode it reads `icon.altMessage` / `icon.altAction`. Built-in messages: `open-url` → `window.open(payload, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")`; `copy-payload` → `$tw.utils.copyToClipboard(payload)` (TW core helper — handles modern Clipboard API + execCommand fallback + emits a tm-notify). If a wikitext action is set, it runs via `invokeViaNavigator` with `<<payload>>`, `<<row-icon-key>>`, `<<row-icon-mode>>` (`"primary"` / `"alt"`), and the standard stage variables. Both message and action fire when both are set. Alt-↵ routes to `primaryRowIcon(item)` (honours `ca-row-icon-primary: yes`, falls back to the first applicable icon). Ctrl-Alt-↵ targets the same icon but with `mode: "alt"` — silently no-ops if the icon declares no alt action, so users who reflex-press it on a primary-only icon don't see surprise behaviour. Clicking an individual glyph fires that specific icon's primary mode and `stopPropagation`s so the row's main selection / fire handler doesn't also run.

! Lenses (row decorations)

A ''lens'' is a global, type-driven decorator that projects one or more //slots// onto each //data row//: ''name'' (replace the displayed name), ''icon'' (a leading glyph), ''annotation'' (a trailing badge). The primitive is the same for every slot: a `ca-lens-<slot>-filter` evaluated per row with `<currentTiddler>` bound to the row's backing tiddler title, whose first non-empty result fills the slot — or a `ca-lens-<slot>-template` (rich wikitext rendered per visible row; `cp-rendering.js#_slotTemplateHtml` caches the output HTML per `(signature, change-count, slot, title)` and re-inserts it via innerHTML, so typing never re-parses; filter wins when both are set). A slot lens may also contribute //actions// via `ca-lens-actions`: `via-entity-type` declares it owns the standard always-on entity-type bridge (the kind lens), any other value is a filter returning action titles to surface on a row — both gated only by `ca-lens-when`, never by slot selection (so turning the kind ''icon'' off keeps kind actions). Actions union into `loadActionsForType` as a fourth path (`cp-lenses.js#_lensContributedActionTitles`). The data model + per-slot choosers live in `widgets/cp-lenses.js`; the merged per-row resolution + cross-render cache in `widgets/cp-row-decorations.js`; the ''Manage lenses'' list rows in `widgets/cp-lens-rows.js`; in-palette authoring in `widgets/cp-lens-editor.js`. This unifies the former ''row-label'' (name) and ''structure-toggle'' (icon) subsystems into one model.

''Lens inheritance (0.0.118).'' Which lens projects a slot is now ''view/channel config'', not a global toggle. A view declares a default lens per slot (`ca-view-lens-name`/`-icon`/`-annotation`); each channel may override (`ca-channel-lens-*`) or inherit; a view may LOCK a slot (`ca-view-locked`) to force its default onto every channel. `cp-views.js#_applyLensInheritance` bakes the effective lens + provenance (`channel.effectiveLens[slot]` / `_lensFrom[slot]`) onto each channel once per view-load, so per-keystroke resolution stays flat. Resolution is therefore ''channel-aware'': `cp-lenses.js#_effectiveLensTitle(slot, item)` reads the row's channel (via `item._layerIdx`) — the same tiddler in two channels can decorate differently — falling back to the active view's default for channel-less rows and, transitionally, to the legacy global lens state. The row-decoration cache (`cp-row-decorations.js`) is keyed by `channel + title` and its signature folds in each channel's effective-lens map. The three former standalone chooser strips were ''removed'' and their choosers relocated into the Structure strip's view→channel tree (a view-default chooser per slot in the view row + a per-channel override chooser, modelled as enum facets so they reuse the whole edit/scratchpad/commit pipeline — `cp-views.js#_lensChooserPills`). New-lens creation lives under ''Manage lenses''.

''Why it exists'' — pre-lenses, two unrelated code paths decided each row's name (''ca-next-scope drill'' synthesised `name: caption || title`; ''view-built row'' applied the view's `ca-view-row-name`), so the same kind-instance appeared as ''Acme Corp'' in ''Find entity'' but `acme/companies/acme-corp` in ''All tiddlers''. A name lens provides one global rule overriding BOTH at render time; icon/annotation generalise the same idea to other slots.

''Registration'' — tiddler tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/lens`'' with a `ca-lens-<slot>-filter` (the projection). Optional `ca-lens-name` / `-chip` / `-hint` / `-help` decorate the chooser pill; `ca-lens-when` is a global existence test (empty result hides the lens — e.g. the Kind lens only when kind types exist); `ca-lens-default` is a space-separated slot list this lens seeds on first load when that slot has no stored pick; `ca-order` sorts. A lens may project several slots and appears in each slot's chooser.

''Shipped lenses'' — three ''name'' lenses: ''Title'' (`[<currentTiddler>]`), ''Caption'' (`[<currentTiddler>get[caption]]` — empty → slot falls back so non-captioned rows keep their default), ''Caption → Title'' (`[<currentTiddler>get[caption]else<currentTiddler>]` — `ca-lens-default: name`). `rimir/kind` ships a ''Kind'' ''icon'' lens (`kind.icon` per instance, gated by `ca-lens-when`).

''Data-row gate'' — `_resolveSlot` short-circuits when `item.dataRow !== true`. The flag is set on ca-next-scope rows (cp-actions) and view rows (cp-views#`_buildRowsForView`) — EXCEPT entries-channel rows (`channel.source === "entries"`), which are palette commands (authored `ca-name` like ''Find entity'') and must never be relabeled to their tiddler title or stamped with a kind glyph. Synthetic ca-items-from rows have empty title and skip. Empty filter result → null → caller uses the intrinsic name / no glyph — rows never render blank.

''State'' — active lens per slot persisted in `$:/state/rimir/cascade-palette/lens/<slot>` (text body). Survives reload, not filesystem-synced. First read with no state seeds the slot's `ca-lens-default` lens. The ''(off)'' / ''(default)'' head pill writes "" to clear the slot.

''Caches'' — (1) lens registry cached on the widget; projecting-lens sets + `ca-lens-when` applicability cached per `wiki.getChangeCount()` so signature computation is O(1) within a render; invalidated by the change-event hook on lens-tag / lens-state changes. (2) `_resolveRowDecorations` caches the merged `{name, icon, annotation}` by row title under a `(selection signature, change-count)` generation — it PERSISTS across keystrokes (typing changes neither), so a projection filter is evaluated ~once per row per data-change, not per keystroke.

''Keyboard'' — the lens choosers are `lens-slot` pills inside the Structure strip (navigated as `viewconfig` pills, not their own Tab sections). Enter/Space cycles the slot's lens (enum-facet edit through `cp-view-editor`'s scratchpad/commit pipeline), ''DEL'' clears it (off / inherit), and ''l'' on a VIEW slot toggles its lock. New lenses are authored from the ''Manage lenses'' entry (NEW_LENS_MESSAGE → `cp-lens-editor#_newLensScratchpad`).

''Authoring'' (`cp-lens-editor.js`) — reuses the scratchpad + `enterEditMode` model: a new lens is a scratch tiddler tagged LENS_TAG under SCRATCHPAD_PREFIX, selected active for live preview while its projection filter is edited (live match-count), then named and saved under `LENS_NS`. Editing clones to scratch; commit overwrites a user lens in place or saves-as-new for a shipped (shadow-only) one. Entry points: the ''➕ New…'' slot pill and the per-slot creator rows of the ''Manage lenses'' list (`NEW_LENS_MESSAGE` with a `slot` param) for the live-preview filter author; and `DELETE_LENS_MESSAGE` from either the DEL-confirm pill or a list row's `ca-on-delete`. ''Per-lens field editor'' — each ''Manage lenses'' row DRILLS into a facet editor built by the `cp-lens-edit-rows` filteroperator (`[cp-lens-edit-rows[<title>]]`): name / chip / when / order (bind-text), default-slot toggles, a ''filter'' + ''template'' bind row per slot, an ''actions'' sub-drill (`cp-lens-actions-rows`: none / via-entity-type / custom filter), and a confirm-gated delete. Because a slot's filter wins over its template, each row's `ca-on-commit` clears its sibling on a non-blank commit (last-edited-wins — committing a template clears the filter, and vice versa; a blank commit promotes the other instead of wiping it), and any pre-existing both-set conflict is marked ''filter ● active'' / ''template ⚠ ignored'' — so the editor never silently ignores a value you set. These are ordinary `ca-bind-*` rows editing a USER lens IN PLACE via the standard menu edit path — so templates and actions are now authored in-palette without hand-editing tiddlers; the cheap filter's live "✓ N matches" feedback stays exclusive to the slot-pill `e` flow (editKind "filter" is JS-only). A SHIPPED (shadow-only) lens can't be edited in place — its drill offers a ''📋 Clone to a custom lens to edit'' leaf (`CLONE_LENS_MESSAGE` → `_cloneLensToUser`) that copies it to `LENS_NS` and reopens the list.

! Footer hint

The bottom strip (`<div class="rcp-hint">`) advertises the gestures available right now. Non-menu sections (input, filter, visibility, preset, view, viewconfig, leader, details, preview) use fixed constants — one string per section — because every gesture in those sections applies uniformly to every pill / cell.

The ''menu'' section composes its hint per-row from `C.HINT_TOKENS` — a flat map of capability-key → token-string. `_composeMenuHint` (in `cascade-palette-widget.js`) reads the selected row plus the current stage and pushes only the tokens that actually do something:

* ''Always present'' — `tab-section`, `fire`, `hold-ctrl-detail`. (`fire` is skipped when no row is selected.)
* ''Gated on stage shape'' — `select` (>1 row), `back` (stack depth >1), `esc-input` vs `esc-tiddler` (`stage.kind === "actions"` swaps in the latter).
* ''Gated on `picked.kind`'' — `toggle`, `edit` (text/number/date), `adjust` (number).
* ''Gated on row capability'' — `drill` (mirrors `drillSelected`'s dispatch shape: `_path`, `_treeContainer + _treeParent`, `entityType + leaf`, `kind=drill + nextScope|itemsFrom`, `isItem + stage.entityType`), `pin` (deep-search row), `actions` (`loadActionsForType(entityType, title)` returns non-empty), `open-icon` (`_rowIcons.length > 0`), `copy-icon` (primary row-icon has `altMessage` / `altAction`).

''Cost'' — every read except the action check is a field on the already-computed `picked` object. The action check reuses `_actionPreviewCountCache` (populated by `_maybeAppendActionPreview` during result render, keyed by `(entityType, title)`, cleared per `renderResults` pass) — most selection changes hit the cache; only views with action-preview disabled fall through to a direct `loadActionsForType` filter call.

''Refresh cadence'' — `_renderHint` is called by `_applyFocusAttr` (Tab / focus change), at the end of `renderResults` (covers arrow nav, input change, stage push / pop, change-event refresh), and at a handful of specific state-change sites in `cp-leaders.js`, `cp-pick-presets.js`, `cp-firing.js`, `cp-input-prefix.js`, and `cp-keyboard.js`. Adding new tokens means extending `_composeMenuHint` only — the call sites already cover every selection-change path.

! Session stack persistence

`close()` paths split into two camps: ''preserve'' (Shift-Esc, action-fire close — including the default close-on-fire via `afterAction`) write the current stack to `$:/temp/rimir/cascade-palette/saved-stack`, and ''reset'' (plain Esc at root, backdrop click, `popStage` past root) clear it. `openPalette()` reads that tiddler on each open; if present, the stack is restored (with `items`/`results` left empty for `recomputeStage` to repopulate); else a fresh root is built. `confirm` and `actions` stages are dropped on serialize — they reference closure-captured strings or a parent-picked tiddler that may be gone — so the saved chain truncates at the first such stage. `openPaletteAtEntry` (and the `OPEN_ENTRY_MESSAGE` handler) pass `{ fresh: true }` to skip restore, since the caller is explicitly pointing at one entry. Filters / visibilities / reaches / fields persist independently across open/close — this channels stack-resume on top.

! Variable substitution

Filter and action wikitext receives a synthetic widget context that exposes:

* `<<query>>` — current input
* `<<picked>>` — the item picked in the current stage (for actions; empty during `ca-next-scope` evaluation)
* `<<parent-picked>>` — the item picked in the parent stage
* `<<stage-N-picked>>` — the item picked at stage index N (root = 0)

The widget assembles these via `buildStageVariables()` walking the stack.

! Navigator routing

The widget mounts in `document.body` via the startup module, so it lives OUTSIDE the page template's main widget subtree. Without intervention, actions invoked from the palette (e.g. `<$action-navigate>`, `tm-edit-tiddler`) would bubble up through the widget's only parent (`$tw.rootWidget`) and stop — never reaching the navigator widget that lives inside the page tree.

The fix lives in `invokeViaNavigator()`: at action-fire time the widget searches `$tw.pageWidgetNode`'s subtree for the navigator (a `<$navigator>` widget) and constructs the action widget tree with the navigator as its parent. Events then bubble naturally into the navigator's handlers.

Falls back to `$tw.rootWidget` if no navigator is found, so messages with global root-level handlers (`tm-save-wiki`, custom messages) still work even without a navigator.

! Action discovery

At every keystroke / stage push, the widget runs cheap filter queries to populate items:

* Entries: `[all[shadows+tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/entry]]`
* Actions for type T: `[all[shadows+tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action]]` filtered to `ca-entity-type === T` ⋃ `ca-entity-type === "*"`

There is no caching — adding/removing action tiddlers takes effect immediately (the next palette open or stage push picks them up). Performance is fine for catalogues of a few hundred tiddlers; if your catalogue grows much larger consider adding a result cache keyed on `wiki.getChangeCount()`.

! Extending

Two kinds of extension:

''Adding cascade edges'' — write entry / action tiddlers in your own plugin or in user tiddler space. Tag with the right tag, set `ca-*` fields, save. No JS, no widget changes. See the ''Protocol'' and ''Examples'' tabs.

''Modifying engine behaviour'' — fork the plugin. The widget is ~500 LOC of self-contained JS. Common extension points: a new stage kind (e.g. ''form'' for multi-field input), a new selection gesture, or a custom item renderer.

! What it does

By default the search input filters the ''current stage's'' visible rows only and matches against each row's `name` and `hint` slots. Three pill strips widen this on independent axes:

* ''Reach'' (teal) — WHERE in the cascade tree to search. Default: local (current stage only).
* ''Meta'' (violet) — WHICH cascade-item author meta keys the matcher reads (the row's display-time slots: `name` / `hint`, plus any author-defined keys). Default: per-row `ca-search-fields`, falling back to global default `name hint`.
* ''Field'' (amber) — WHICH literal tiddler fields the matcher reads on the row's backing tiddler (`text` / `caption` / `tags` / author-defined). Default: not consulted unless a Field pill is pushed.

All three strips use the same push / remove / DEL / navigate grammar as the existing Filter and Visibility strips. Strips appear only when at least one pill is pushed — unless you toggle Settings → ''Pin all pill rows'' (0.0.87+), which keeps every strip visible as a dev / discoverability aid.

! Reach strip — WHERE to search

|!Pill |!Leader |!Effect |
|🔍 Here |`d` |Walk every reachable drill under the currently-visible stage. |
|🌐 Everywhere |`g` |Walk every reachable drill under the active view's root. The drill stack stays put — the pill widens the search frontier, it doesn't move you. |

The two Reach pills are ''mutually exclusive'' — pushing one evicts the other. Only one scope is ever active. DEL on the focused pill removes it (returning to local search).

When a Reach pill is active, results carry a breadcrumb prefix (`Kinds → Task → fields  priority: enum`) naming the drill chain from the search anchor to the matched row.

! Meta strip — WHICH cascade-item author meta keys

Pills tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta`''. Each declares a `ca-meta-key` naming the cascade-item property the matcher reads.

|!Pill |!`ca-meta-key` |!Source |!Visible inline? |
|🏷 Name |`name` |`ca-name` on entries; synthesised from `caption` → path-segment → title on tiddler-backed rows |Yes — the row's title. Inline match highlight. |
|💡 Hint |`hint` |`ca-hint` on entries (empty on tiddler-backed rows without an explicit ca-hint) |Yes — the row's subtitle. Inline match highlight. |

Multiple Meta pills can coexist. When any are active, the matcher reads the UNION of those slots, ignoring per-row `ca-search-fields` and the global default. No Meta pills active → matcher uses each row's `ca-search-fields` declaration, falling back to the global default at ''`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/search-fields-default`'' (ships `name hint`).

! Field strip — WHICH literal tiddler fields

Pills tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field`''. Each declares a `ca-tiddler-field` naming the tiddler field the matcher reads on the row's backing tiddler.

|!Pill |!`ca-tiddler-field` |!Source |
|📄 Text |`text` |The backing tiddler's `text` field — the wikitext / content body. |

Multiple Field pills can coexist; the matcher unions them. Synthetic rows (no backing tiddler) silently skip every Field pill. No Field pills active → the matcher skips the tiddler-field channel entirely (default keeps search fast).

''Leader `a`'' pushes all six shipped search pills at once (five Meta + one Field) — equivalent to "match anywhere".

! Authoring custom Meta pills

Ship a tiddler tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta`'' that names a cascade-item property the matcher should consult. Example — a `caption` pill for the row's display name (only useful if you populate `item.caption` somewhere; usually you'd ship a Field pill instead):

```
title: $:/config/myplugin/search-meta/displayname
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta
ca-meta-key: displayname
ca-chip: 🪧 Display name
ca-hint: Match against the row's displayname slot.
ca-order: 160
```

! Authoring custom Field pills

Ship a tiddler tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field`'' that names a tiddler field the matcher should read on each row's backing tiddler. Example — a `caption` pill for the tiddler's caption field:

```
title: $:/config/myplugin/search-field/caption
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field
ca-tiddler-field: caption
ca-chip: 🪧 Caption
ca-hint: Match against the tiddler's caption field.
ca-order: 110
```

Array-typed fields (`tags`, list-fields) are flattened to space-separated strings before substring matching, so a Field pill on `tags` matches `urgen` against `tags: work urgent`.

! Multi-match visualization

When a row matches in multiple slots (e.g. Name AND Description, or Description AND Text), each match contributes:

* Inline highlight on the visible name / hint slot (whichever matched).
* One snippet line per non-displayed match (`text`, or any author-defined key the matcher consulted), shown beneath the row with the matched pill's chip label + 24 chars of context before + the matched substring (highlighted) + 40 chars after.

So a single row can carry inline highlight AND multiple snippets — the user sees every reason the row is in the result list. The snippet caption reads the pill's chip ("📝 Description") rather than the bare slot name, so labels stay readable.

! Picking a deep result — three gestures

When a Reach pill is active, results carry a `_path` array (the drill chain from the anchor). Picking a result replays the path so the cascade lands at the row's natural parent. Three gestures distinguish what happens next:

|!Gesture |!Effect |
|''Enter'' |Replay path + execute (fire leaves, drill into drills). |
|''Right-arrow'' |Replay path + drill (no-op on plain leaves). |
|''Space'' |''Pin only'' — replay path, select the row at its natural stage, but do NOT fire / edit / open the action menu. Safe inspection gesture for destructive matches. |

Any `<<parent-picked>>` / `<<stage-N-picked>>` context the row's actions depend on resolves the same way as a manual drill.

! Authoring searchable text on cascade items

The shipped Meta pills read `name` and `hint` only. To make additional searchable content available on a row, author a custom Meta pill (see above) that names whichever cascade-item property you want exposed, and stamp that property onto items in your row-builder. Two opt-out / per-row controls remain on the protocol:

```
ca-search-fields: name hint   (per-row override of the searched meta keys)
ca-search-skip: yes           (exclude from deep walk)
```

''`ca-search-skip: yes`'' opts a row out of deep search results AND prevents its subtree from being descended. Useful for `+ Add new` input prompts whose name only makes sense in their immediate context. Default auto-skip applies to `text`, `number`, `date`, `toggle`, and `confirm` row kinds.

! Caps

The walk is bounded — no walk is ever unbounded — by three hard caps (config tiddler defaults):

|!Config |!Default |!What it does |
|`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/deep-search-max-depth` |4 |Maximum drill depth from the search anchor |
|`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/deep-search-max-nodes` |800 |Total items visited before the walk aborts |
|`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/deep-search-max-ms` |80 |Wall-clock time per keystroke before the walk aborts |

When any cap fires, the result list ends with a ''truncation hint row'' so you know to refine the query.

! Sending the messages programmatically

A toolbar button, sidebar item, or any external wikitext can push pills via the same widget messages the leaders use:

```
<$action-sendmessage $message="rimir-cascade-palette-add-reach"
  reach="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/reach/here"/>

<$action-sendmessage $message="rimir-cascade-palette-add-meta"
  meta="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta/name"/>

<$action-sendmessage $message="rimir-cascade-palette-add-field"
  field="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field/text"/>
```

`rimir-cascade-palette-reset-reach` / `-reset-meta` / `-reset-fields` clear the respective strips.

! Migration from 0.0.87 and earlier

The old single Search-in strip is gone. Pills used to be tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field`'' (or the pre-0.0.84 legacy ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/field`'') with a single `ca-field-name` field. Both schemas are no longer honoured.

* Pills that read a cascade-item author meta key (anything except `text`) move to the Meta strip — retag to ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta`'' and rename `ca-field-name` → `ca-meta-key`.
* Pills that read a literal tiddler field (only `text` among the shipped ones) stay on the Field strip — keep the tag, rename `ca-field-name` → `ca-tiddler-field`.
* `ca-field-chip` / `ca-field-hint` / `ca-field-help` rename to `ca-chip` / `ca-hint` / `ca-help` in both strips.
* The leader `a` still pushes every shipped pill — but now via two messages (`add-meta` for each Meta pill, `add-field` for each Field pill).

The diagnostics drill ''Deprecations'' (under Configurations) lists any tiddlers still on the legacy schema.

! Limitations (MVP)

* Action menus are not walked. Search lists the entity rows themselves; drilling into an action menu is a separate gesture.
* No per-keystroke memo cache yet — each keystroke recomputes the walk. Caps keep this fast on real-world trees.
* Result ranking is BFS-natural (shallower matches first; same-depth keeps cascade's sort). Exact-match boost and other ranking are on the roadmap.
* Pills don't persist across sessions or get saved into Presets yet — they're session-local. Preset integration is on the roadmap.
* No ''+ Add Meta / + Add Field'' picker pill yet (à la Presets' `+` save pill) — pills are pushed only via leaders or external messages for now.

! Authoring a contribution

Cascade-palette is engineered to be extended by ''one tiddler per cascade edge''. The vast majority of integrations never touch JavaScript. Pick the right tag, set the right `ca-*` fields, save — restart only if you also added a JS module (filter operator, widget, startup).

|!You want to add… |!Tag the tiddler with… |!Required fields |!See worked examples in |
|A new menu entry (root stage) |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/entry` |`ca-name`, `ca-kind`, plus `ca-actions` (leaf) or `ca-next-scope` (drill) |[[Protocol|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol]] §"Worked example 1–4" (or create it in-palette: ''Manage entries'' → ''+ New entry…'') |
|A new action for an entity type |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action` |`ca-name`, `ca-kind`, `ca-entity-type` and/or `ca-applies` |[[Protocol]] §"Worked example 3–5" (or create it in-palette: ''Manage actions'' → ''+ New action…'') |
|A new search-filter pill |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/filter` |`ca-filter-name`, `ca-filter-expr` |[[Protocol]] §"Worked example — Title-prefix filter" |
|A new visibility (hide-predicate) pill |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/visibility` |`ca-visibility-name`, `ca-visibility-expr` |[[Protocol]] §"Worked example — Hide a group" |
|A new view (root-stage strategy) |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view` |`ca-view-name`, `ca-view-roots` |[[Protocol]] §"Views" |
|A new channel (sub-component of a view) |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/channel` |`ca-channel-name`, `ca-channel-roots` |[[Protocol]] §"Multi-channel views" |
|A new grouping axis |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/axis` |`ca-axis-name`, `ca-axis-key` |[[Protocol]] §"Axes" (or create it in-palette: ''Manage axes'' → ''+ New axis…'') |
|A new leader-key gesture |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/leader` |`ca-leader-key`, `ca-leader-actions` |[[Protocol]] §"Leader keys" |
|A new side-preview template |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/side-preview` |`ca-preview-applies` or `ca-preview-context`, body wikitext |[[Protocol]] §"Side preview" |
|A new row icon |`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/row-icon` |`ca-row-icon-applies`, `ca-row-icon-glyph`, action/message |[[Protocol]] §"Row icons" |

If you find yourself wishing for a tag or field that doesn't exist, you're probably looking for a new ''kind of cascade primitive'' — please open an issue rather than patching the widget. The widget aims to be a constant; the protocol is the extension surface.

! Local dev cycle

You're editing tiddlers in `dev-wiki/`. The filesystem-watcher plugin (also rimir) picks up changes in `dev-wiki/tiddlers/` and `dev-wiki/plugins/`. Everything declarative is hot — close & reopen the palette to pick up new entries / actions / leaders / axes / filters / visibility / views / channels / side-previews / row-icons.

JS modules (`widgets/cp-*.js`, custom filter operators, startup modules) are NOT hot — restart the wiki server:

```
# from project root, manually
node node_modules/tiddlywiki/tiddlywiki.js dev-wiki --listen
```

Or use `bin/tw start`.

! Discovering what's loaded — the Diagnostics drill

Open the palette → ''Configurations'' → ''Diagnostics''. Three drills:

* ''Loaded actions'' — every action tiddler the engine sees. Use this to verify your action is tagged correctly and its `ca-entity-type` / `ca-applies` resolves.
* ''Loaded entries'' — every entry tiddler. Use this to spot a stray `ca-position-<view>` that demotes your entry to the wrong place.
* ''Loaded settings'' — every `setting`-tagged tiddler. Use this when a new setting row isn't appearing in the Settings menu.

The diagnostic drills are filter-driven — adding more diagnostic listings is just one more entry tiddler with a `ca-next-scope` filter.

! Debugging action discovery

When an action doesn't appear where you expect:

# Open the palette, navigate to the target row.
# Hit Space — if you see ''empty list, no actions'', the engine found zero applicable actions for this row.
# Three discovery paths are unioned and deduplicated:
## ''Catalogue'' — does the action's `ca-entity-type` match the row's bound `entityType`? (Bound by `ca-channel-row-entity-type` on the emitting channel.)
## ''Configured-field bridge'' — is `$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/entity-type-field` set to a field, AND does the row's tiddler have that field's value matching the action's `ca-entity-type`? (E.g. `rimir/kind` sets it to `kind.type`.)
## ''Filter'' — when the action declares `ca-applies`, does the filter return non-empty for `<currentTiddler>` = row title?
# Every discovered action is then narrowed by its `ca-action-when` (if set) — same `<currentTiddler>` binding.
# Open the browser console — `ca-applies` / `ca-action-when` evaluation errors are logged (no silent failures).

! Backwards-compat conventions

When evolving the protocol, never break authored tiddlers. The plugin's track record:

* ''Aliases.'' `ca-view-source` is honoured as a back-compat alias for `ca-view-roots`. Pattern: read the new field first; fall back to the old one. Document the alias in `doc/protocol.tid` and `doc/reference.tid`.
* ''Phased rollout.'' When a complex refactor is needed (e.g. the 0.0.37 → 0.0.38 multi-channel view model), ship the new primitives first with back-compat, then rewrite the engine on top in the next version. Two-phase landings keep risk down.
* ''Soft deprecation'' — when an old form should no longer be used, emit a one-time `console.warn` via `cp.deprecationWarning(key, message)` (cp-utils.js). Never per-keystroke; never silent removal. Surface active deprecations in the ''Diagnostics → Deprecations'' sub-entry so users find them without reading the changelog.

! Versioning

''Default bump is patch'' (`+0.0.1`). Bump minor/major only when the user explicitly asks. After any visible change, also add a row to `changelog.tid` (`|!Version |!Date |!Changes |` table).

! Testing your additions

Cascade-palette is the prime ''extending another plugin'' reference plugin — so testing your authoring channel matters. Two patterns work without touching JS:

''CLI gotchas fixture'' (`tw-tests/gotchas/fixtures/<your-slug>/`) — small standalone wiki with `tiddlywiki.info` loading cascade-palette + your contribution, `tiddlers/RunTest.tid` rendering a representative filter (e.g. action discovery for a specific entity type, or position resolution for an entry), and `expected.txt` capturing the byte-stable output. Run with `bin/tw test:gotchas <your-slug>`. Bootstrap `expected.txt` via `UPDATE=1 ./tw-tests/gotchas/run.sh <your-slug>`.

''Wiki test spec'' — for authoring-channel behaviour like cascade-position-fallback or filter substitution semantics, write a tiddler tagged `$:/tags/wiki-test-spec` in `tw-tests/test-edition/tiddlers/` with `Setup`, `Description`, `ExpectedResult`, and `Narrative` sections. See [[tw-gotchas-testing#Wiki-based test ExpectedResult…]] for the trailing-newline trap.

''Jasmine spec'' (`tw-tests/test-edition/tests/cascade-palette/*.spec.js`) — for pure-function unit tests of any JS utility you contribute (e.g. a new sort comparator, a sanitisation helper). Run with `bin/tw test cascade-palette`.

! What lives where (engine source layout)

```
dev-wiki/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/
├── plugin.info
├── widgets/
│   ├── cascade-palette-widget.js   # orchestrator: state + render + render + lifecycle
│   ├── cascade-palette-startup.js  # mounts widget in document.body at boot
│   ├── cp-constants.js             # tag names, message strings, defaults
│   ├── cp-filter-ops.js            # custom filter operator(s)
│   └── cp-*.js                     # subsystem libraries (each patches the prototype)
├── actions/, entries/, axes/, views/, channels/, filters/, visibility/, leaders/, reach/, row-icons/, settings/
│                                   # shipped declarative content
├── config/                         # raw $:/config/... tiddlers (engine-facing)
├── diagnostics/                    # entries that drill into loaded-* lists
├── doc/                            # doc-template doc tiddlers (you are here)
├── field/                          # search-in-field pill tiddlers (not ca-bind-field!)
├── help/                           # in-app help tiddlers
├── templates/                      # detail templates
├── styles.tid, icon.tid, readme.tid, changelog.tid, settings.tid, …
```

For engine internals (how the widget actually works), see [[TW Internals|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/tw-internals]].

! See also

* [[Protocol|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol]] — authoritative authoring guide
* [[Reference|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/reference]] — exhaustive field reference
* [[Architecture|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/architecture]] — high-level component map
* [[TW Internals|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/tw-internals]] — TW-specific internals (navigator routing, fake widgets, startup ordering, …)
