! Presets

A ''preset'' captures the current `(active-view, filters, visibility)` under a name. Apply a preset to replay that state in one step. Tag: ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/preset`''.

Fields on a preset tiddler:

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`ca-preset-name` |Display name (e.g. "PersonsOfA") |
|`ca-preset-view` |Title of the view active at save time |
|`ca-preset-constraints` |JSON object `{"filters": [{title, arg}, …], "visibility": [{title, arg}, …]}` — both constraint lists at save time |
|`ca-order` |Sort key in the preset strip |

! Save flow (`s` leader)

# Press `s`, wait 500ms.
# The input is repurposed for one-line name entry — placeholder ''"Save preset as…"'', input picks up an emerald background.
# Type a name, press Enter. The widget writes a preset tiddler at ''`$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/presets/<sanitised-slug>`''. If a tiddler at that title already exists, ''`-2`'', ''`-3`'', … are appended.
# Esc cancels.

! Recall flow (`r` leader)

# Press `r`, wait 500ms.
# Focus jumps to the preset pill strip at the top of the popup.
# Use `←` / `→` to select a preset, Enter to apply. The palette: clears current filters + visibility, pushes the preset's filters and visibility rules (looked up by title), switches to the preset's view.

If a preset references a deleted constraint tiddler, that constraint is skipped (warning to console). If it references a deleted view, the palette stays on its current view and rebuilds with the new constraint state. No data loss — presets are inspectable as regular tiddlers.

! Side preview pane

An entry/action can register a ''side preview'' that opens a right-column pane when the user drills into the row. The cascade column visually shrinks to 50% on the left; the pane renders an authored wikitext template against an entry-computed context. The pane stays visible while the drilled stage (or any deeper one) is on the stack, and disappears once the user pops back out — so the cascade fills 100% again.

Distinct from the ''detail'' drawer (Ctrl-hold or `details-always-on`): the detail drawer is bound to the currently-selected row and renders templates tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/template`''. The side preview is bound to ''what the user is editing'' — pinned at drill-time and kept stable as the user navigates inside.

! Two registration mechanisms (use either, or both)

! ! (a) Per-menu — declare on the entry/action

;`ca-preview-template`
:Title of a wikitext tiddler whose body is rendered in the right pane. Required to enable an explicit candidate.
;`ca-preview-context`
:Filter evaluated at drill-time in the parent stage's substitution scope (`<<picked>>`, `<<parent-picked>>`, `<<query>>`, `<<context-tiddler>>`, etc.). The first result becomes `<<currentTiddler>>` inside the preview template AND is exposed to deeper stages' substitution scope as `<<stage-preview-context>>`. Defaults to `<<picked>>` (the row being drilled into) — typical for actions where `<<picked>>` is the entity being acted upon.
;`ca-preview-title`
:Optional caption shown in the colored title strip above the preview body. Empty value keeps the strip hidden.
;`ca-preview-name`
:Optional pill label when multiple candidates are visible at once. Default derived from the template title.
;`ca-preview-per-row`
:When `yes`, the active context tracks the currently-selected row's title — live ↑/↓ updates. Used by browse lists.

''Tag-only opt-in.'' If you want the side-preview pane to activate but don't have a specific template in mind, omit `ca-preview-template` and set just `ca-preview-context` (or `ca-preview-per-row: yes`). The pane will populate purely from ''tag-based candidates'' (below) that match the resolved context. Useful for entity-browsing entries that want auto-attached previews.

''Auto-open.'' Since 0.0.100 you usually don't need either of those opt-ins: every view auto-opens the pane on rows whose title matches a tag-based candidate's `ca-preview-applies` filter, unless the view sets ''`ca-view-show-side-preview: no`''. Reach for the explicit per-menu / opt-in fields when you want a specific template pinned regardless of tag matches, when you want a fixed-context (non-per-row) preview, or when you want the pane to open even without any tag match.

! ! (b) Tag-based — declare a self-contained template + applicability filter

Any tiddler tagged ''`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/side-preview`'' is a candidate that auto-attaches to the preview pane whenever the active context matches its `ca-preview-applies` filter. The tagged tiddler is BOTH the registration AND (by default) the template body — no separate template tiddler needed.

;`ca-preview-applies`
:Filter evaluated with `<currentTiddler>` bound to the active context. Returns non-empty → this candidate applies. Empty / missing = always applies (rarely what you want).
;`ca-preview-template`
:Optional override pointing at a separate template tiddler. Defaults to the tagged tiddler's own title.
;`ca-preview-name`
:Pill label. Default derived from the template title.
;`ca-preview-title`
:Optional caption shown in the colored title strip above the body.
;`ca-preview-order`
:Sort key among tag candidates. Default `100`. Lower = earlier.

When per-menu and tag-based mechanisms BOTH contribute candidates against the same context, all candidates show as pills in a horizontal row at the top of the pane (per-menu first, then tag candidates by `ca-preview-order`). The active pill is highlighted. ←/→ when focus is on the preview cycles between them (also click). With a single candidate the pill row is suppressed entirely.

! ! (c) Channel / view "Overview" rows — a summary you focus

A channel or view can declare a ''summary'' template that the cascade surfaces as a dedicated, focusable row rather than a tag match:

;`ca-channel-preview` / `ca-view-preview`
:Title of a wikitext tiddler. When set, the ''root stage'' emits one synthetic ''Overview'' row — for a channel it leads that channel's group; for a view it leads the whole result list, grouped under the view name.
;`ca-channel-preview-name` / `ca-view-preview-name`
:Label for the Overview row and its preview pill. Default `Overview`.
;`ca-channel-preview-title` / `ca-view-preview-title`
:Caption shown in the title strip above the preview body.

The Overview row is a ''non-drill no-op leaf'', excluded from search, pinned to the top of its group. ''Focusing'' it (↑/↓) renders the template in the side preview — this works because a selected row's own `ca-preview-template` now drives the pane (not only a drilled one). ''Enter'' on the row moves focus into the preview pane so you can scroll / interact. Overview rows appear only at the root stage, never in drilled sub-stages, and are suppressed when the view sets `ca-view-show-side-preview: no`. The template renders with no particular `<<currentTiddler>>` context (it's a fixed summary), so author it against global filters.

tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action
ca-entity-type: kind
ca-name: Edit fields
ca-kind: drill
ca-items-from: [function[kind.cascade-fields-for-edit],<parent-picked>]
ca-next-title: Fields of <<parent-picked>>
ca-preview-template: $:/plugins/example/templates/kind-form-preview
ca-preview-context: [<picked>]

```
title: $:/plugins/example/templates/kind-form-preview
type: text/vnd.tiddlywiki

! Form for <<currentTiddler>>

A form rendered from this kind's current field set. As you add / remove / edit fields in the cascade, this preview re-renders live.

<$transclude tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/kind/view"/>
```

Drilling into "Edit fields" pushes the field-edit stage AND attaches the preview. Each time the user edits the kind tiddler (the context — its `kind.fields` array changes), the wiki change-hook invalidates the cache and the pane re-renders.

! Lifecycle

* Preview attaches when the user drills via Right-arrow / Enter / Space into a row that carries `ca-preview-template`.
* While the registering stage is anywhere on the stack, the pane stays visible.
* Drilling DEEPER (pushing another stage) inherits the same preview — `<<stage-preview-context>>` is the resolved context.
* Popping past the registering stage hides the pane and restores the cascade to 100%.
* If a deeper stage ALSO declares `ca-preview-template`, that one takes over while it's on the stack (topmost wins).
* Closing the palette clears the preview cache entirely.

! Focus & interactivity

The pane joins the Tab cycle as a new focus section ''`preview`'' (only when visible). Esc returns to input; arrow-up/down let the browser scroll natively. Mousedown on the pane background grabs focus, but clicks on form inputs / buttons / links inside the rendered template pass through — the template is fully interactive.

! Limitations & follow-ups

* ''Editing presets'' — no in-palette UI for rename / delete. Use the wiki normally (preset tiddlers are real tiddlers).
* ''Compose presets'' — applying a preset always ''replaces'' both constraint lists. There's no "apply on top of existing state".
* ''Side-preview tabs'' — only a single preview template per entry/action right now. Tag-based discovery (à la detail templates) is a possible follow-up if multiple plugins want to register competing previews on the same drill.

! Row icons (`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/row-icon`)

A row-icon is a small glyph rendered in a footer strip below the main line of any tiddler-bearing row. Use it to surface affordances on the row's backing tiddler — opening an external URL, jumping to an attachment, copying a value, etc. — without crowding the name / value slots. The strip renders only when at least one icon resolves for the row; rows with no applicable icons look identical to before.

! ! Built-in: URL icon

The plugin ships ''`row-icons/url.tid`'' (key `url`) that surfaces a ''🌐'' glyph on any row whose backing tiddler carries a URL value in one of the configured fields. The scanned field list lives at ''`$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/url-fields`'' — default `url`, space-separated for multiple (e.g. `url website homepage`). The first field whose value matches ''`/^(?:https?|ftp|ftps|mailto|tel):/i`'' wins; trailing whitespace is trimmed.

Two gestures on the same row:

* ''Alt-↵'' (or click the glyph) opens the URL in a new browser tab — `window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")`.
* ''Ctrl-Alt-↵'' copies the URL to the clipboard via `$tw.utils.copyToClipboard(url)` (TW core helper — handles both the modern Clipboard API and the legacy `execCommand` fallback, emits a tm-notify on success / failure).

The row's normal Enter / Ctrl-Enter behaviour is unchanged.

! ! Author your own

Tag a tiddler with `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/row-icon` and declare:

;`ca-row-icon-key`
:Symbolic id (`url`, `attachment`, `linear-ticket`, ...). The key `url` triggers the built-in field-scanning resolver. Other keys must declare `ca-row-icon-applies` (the gate) + optionally `ca-row-icon-payload` (the value bound to `<<payload>>` when the icon fires).
;`ca-row-icon-glyph`
:Display character / emoji. Default `•`.
;`ca-row-icon-hint`
:Tooltip on hover. The runtime appends ` · Alt-↵ or click` so the gesture is discoverable.
;`ca-row-icon-applies`
:Filter — `<currentTiddler>` is the row's tiddler title. Non-empty result = the icon shows. Required for non-`url` keys.
;`ca-row-icon-payload`
:Optional filter — first result is bound to `<<payload>>` when the icon fires. Use this when your action wants to act on a specific field's value rather than the tiddler title.
;`ca-row-icon-action`
:Optional wikitext actions. Fired with `<<payload>>` + `<<row-icon-key>>` + the standard stage variables (`<<picked>>`, `<<parent-picked>>`, `<<currentTiddler>>` bound to the row).
;`ca-row-icon-message`
:Optional built-in JS dispatch key for the ''primary'' gesture (Alt-↵ / click). Currently recognised: `open-url` (`window.open(payload, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")`), `copy-payload` (`$tw.utils.copyToClipboard(payload)`). May coexist with `ca-row-icon-action` (both fire).
;`ca-row-icon-alt-action`
:Optional wikitext actions fired by the ''secondary'' gesture — ''Ctrl-Alt-↵'' on the row. Receives the same variables as `ca-row-icon-action` plus `<<row-icon-mode>>: "alt"` (so a single action can branch on which gesture fired it).
;`ca-row-icon-alt-message`
:Optional built-in JS dispatch key for the secondary gesture. Same vocabulary as `ca-row-icon-message`. The shipped 🌐 icon uses `copy-payload` here to put the URL on the clipboard.
;`ca-row-icon-alt-hint`
:Tooltip text for the secondary gesture. Shown on a second line of the glyph's hover tooltip suffixed with `· Ctrl-Alt-↵`.
;`ca-row-icon-primary`
:`yes` = preferred target for the row-level ''Alt-↵'' keyboard gesture when multiple icons apply. If no icon is `primary`, the first applicable icon (by `ca-row-icon-order`) wins.
;`ca-row-icon-order`
:Display order in the strip (lower first, default `100`).

! ! Worked example — Linear ticket link

```
title: $:/plugins/example/row-icons/linear
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/row-icon
ca-row-icon-key: linear
ca-row-icon-glyph: 🔗
ca-row-icon-hint: Open Linear ticket
ca-row-icon-applies: [<currentTiddler>has[linear-ticket]]
ca-row-icon-payload: [<currentTiddler>get[linear-ticket]addprefix[https://linear.app/team/issue/]]
ca-row-icon-message: open-url
ca-row-icon-order: 20
```

Any tiddler carrying a `linear-ticket` field gets a 🔗 in its row-icon strip. Alt-↵ (or clicking the glyph) constructs the URL and opens it in a new tab.

! ! Worked example — Wiki-internal action

```
title: $:/plugins/example/row-icons/edit-raw
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/row-icon
ca-row-icon-key: edit-raw
ca-row-icon-glyph: ✎
ca-row-icon-hint: Open the raw editor
ca-row-icon-applies: [<currentTiddler>!is[system]]
ca-row-icon-action: <$action-sendmessage $message="tm-edit-tiddler" $param=<<currentTiddler>>/>
```

Surfaces a ✎ on every non-system tiddler; Alt-↵ fires `tm-edit-tiddler` via the navigator.

! Reach pills (`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/reach`)

Reach pills configure WHERE the search input walks. Same push / remove / DEL grammar as filter and visibility pills, just a separate strip with its own tag family and a teal accent. A reach-tagged tiddler declares:

;`ca-reach-name`
:Display name in the help pane.
;`ca-reach-mode`
:`here` (walk the subtree under the current stage) or `everywhere` (walk from the active view's root). Reach pills are ''mutually exclusive'' — pushing any reach pill evicts every other reach pill, so only one scope is ever active.
;`ca-reach-chip`
:Plain-text pill label. Defaults to the reach-name.
;`ca-reach-hint` / `ca-reach-help`
:Hover tooltip / details-pane help.

''Push via:'' the ''`rimir-cascade-palette-add-reach`'' message with param ''`reach: <tiddler-title>`''. Leaders d / g are the shipped shortcuts.

! Search-meta pills (`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta`)

Search-meta pills configure WHICH cascade-item author meta keys the matcher reads (the row's `name`, `hint`, and any author-defined slots populated by cp-items.js or a custom row-builder). Same grammar as reach pills, separate strip, violet accent. A pill-tagged tiddler declares:

;`ca-meta-key`
:The cascade-item property the pill represents (e.g. `name`, `hint`, or any author-defined key the cascade-item builder populates).
;`ca-chip` / `ca-hint` / `ca-help`
:Display chip / tooltip / details-pane help.

When at least one Search-meta pill is active, the matcher walks the UNION of those meta keys, ignoring per-row `ca-search-fields` and global default. No meta pills active → matcher uses each row's `ca-search-fields` declaration, falling back to global default at `$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/search-fields-default`.

''Push via:'' ''`rimir-cascade-palette-add-meta`'' with param ''`meta: <tiddler-title>`''.

! Search-field pills (`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field`)

Search-field pills configure WHICH literal tiddler fields the matcher reads on the row's backing tiddler. Same grammar as reach / meta pills, separate strip, amber accent. Synthetic rows (no backing tiddler) silently skip every Field pill. A pill-tagged tiddler declares:

;`ca-tiddler-field`
:The tiddler field name to read via `wiki.getTiddler(item.title).fields[<name>]`. Any field works: `text`, `caption`, `tags`, `modifier`, author-defined.
;`ca-chip` / `ca-hint` / `ca-help`
:Same shape as Meta.

Array-typed fields (like `tags`) are flattened to a space-separated string before substring matching.

When at least one Search-field pill is active, the matcher unions the tiddler-field channel with the meta channel. No field pills active → the tiddler-field channel is skipped entirely (keeps the default search cheap).

''Push via:'' ''`rimir-cascade-palette-add-field`'' with param ''`field: <tiddler-title>`''.

! Item-level search authoring (`ca-search-*` on cascade items)

;`ca-search-fields`
:Space-separated list of cascade-item meta keys the matcher walks for THIS row. Default per global config.
;`ca-search-skip`
:When `yes`, the deep walker excludes this row from results AND does not descend its subtree. Default auto-skip applies to `text`, `number`, `date`, `toggle`, and `confirm` row kinds.

Authoring example:

```
title: $:/plugins/example/entries/find-things
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/entry
ca-name: Find things
ca-hint: Search across projects, tasks, notes.
ca-kind: drill
ca-next-scope: [tag[work]]
```

! In-palette help (`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help`)

Help sections are tiddlers tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help`. They appear as rows in the ''Help'' entry (also reachable via the `?` leader). Each row's body wikitext renders in the side preview as the user navigates ↑/↓ — this is the standard `ca-preview-template` machinery with `ca-preview-per-row: yes`.

''Schema'' (standard cascade-item fields — no `ca-help-*` namespace):

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`ca-name` |Display name in the row |
|`ca-icon` |Glyph |
|`ca-group` |Category for visual grouping in the Help drill. Use `Plugin: <slug>` to land in the ''Plugins'' sub-drill. |
|`ca-order` |Sort order (lower first) |
|`ca-hint` |One-line subtitle (shown in the row's hint slot) |
|`ca-kind` |`leaf` (default) or `drill`. Drills declare their own `ca-next-scope`. |
|`text` |Wikitext body rendered in the side preview |

''Where to put the tiddler'':

* ''In a plugin'' — `$:/plugins/<author>/<plugin>/help` (one tiddler per plugin convention).
* ''In a wiki'' — any title works.

''Worked example — a plugin contribution'':

```
title: $:/plugins/example/help
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help
ca-name: example
ca-icon: 🧪
ca-group: Plugin: example
ca-order: 10
ca-hint: What the example plugin adds to the palette.

|!Adds |!Activation |
|`x` leader |drills into Examples |
|`Examples` entry |root-level browser |

→ Full docs: <$link to="$:/plugins/example/doc/overview">example overview</$link>
```

Plugin-contributed leaders / pills / entries already appear automatically in the core ''Keys'' / ''Pills'' / ''Entries'' help sections via `<$list filter="...">` over the existing protocol tags — the per-plugin help tiddler is just narrative context.

! Limitations & follow-ups

* ''Editing presets'' — no in-palette UI for rename / delete. Use the wiki normally (preset tiddlers are real tiddlers).
* ''Compose presets'' — only one preset at a time.
* ''Action-menu walking'' — deep search doesn't currently descend into action menus, only entity and drill rows. Authors who want actions reachable from search can wire them via `ca-items-from` synthetic rows.
* ''Per-keystroke memo cache'' — each keystroke recomputes the deep walk; caps keep this fast. A memo invalidated by the wiki change hook is on the roadmap.
* ''Result ranking'' — deep results are in BFS-natural order (shallower matches first; same-depth keeps the cascade's sort). Exact-match boost and other ranking are Phase 2.

! Focus model

The palette is one popup with up to eight focusable sections, partitioned into two groups:

* ''pills group'' (top of the palette, visually stacked): ''preset'' (always present — trailing ''+'' pill is the save-as affordance even when no presets exist), ''visibility'' (only when ≥ 1 visibility rule active), ''filter'' (only when ≥ 1 filter active), ''view'' (only when ≥ 2 views declared), ''structure'' (always present when the active view declares any channels), ''leader'' (only when ≥ 1 leader is visible for the active view — see leader scoping below). (As of 0.0.118 the three standalone row-decoration ''lens'' chooser strips are gone — they're relocated into the Structure strip's view→channel tree, see below.) The structure strip has a ''two-stage'' interaction model: on focus it shows a ''compact'' summary row (view name, channel count + composition, view-scoped pills sort/entries/grouping); pressing ''Enter / Space / →'' expands it to the full stacked layout. Expanded, the ''view'' row leads with three lens choosers — ''Name'' / ''Icon'' / ''Note'' — editing the view's default decoration lens per slot (`l` toggles a slot ''lock''); each ''channel'' row (indented under the view) leads with its own three choosers overriding or inheriting the view default (showing ''(inherit view)'' / 🔒 cues), followed by the channel's primitive pills (roots/children/leaf/label + row decorations + entity-type). A lens chooser cycles its lenses on ↵/Space and clears on DEL; new lenses are created via ''Manage lenses''. Built-in channels (the synthetic ''entries'' channel auto-appended to tree views) render muted to flag their automatic nature. ''Esc'' from expanded collapses back to compact; ''Esc'' from compact refocuses input. The leader strip surfaces every visible leader as a ''[key] name'' pill — same activation as the typed-gesture path (key + idle), but discoverable without prior knowledge. Leaders may opt into per-view scope via ''`ca-leader-views`'' (empty = global).
* ''main group'': ''input'' (search box), ''menu'' (result list), ''detail'' (Ctrl-hold drawer below the menu, only when open), ''preview'' (right-column pane, only when an entry/action on the stack registered a ''`ca-preview-template`'').

The active section gets the browser-level focus and a visual cue; keyboard gestures route accordingly. ''Tab'' cycles within the current group; ''Shift-Tab'' jumps between groups, restoring the focus you last held in the group you're entering (the menu row you were on, the filter pill you were editing, etc.); it falls back to the bottom-most pill (entering pills) or input (returning to main) when that slot has since disappeared or was never visited. ''↑ / ↓'' inside the pill group walks vertically across rows — ↑ from input enters pills at the bottom-most row, ↓ from the bottom-most pill drops back into input. ''Esc'' walks the stack back one step keystroke-by-keystroke: in input or menu focus it pops the current stage at any depth > 1, and from a pill section it returns focus to input. At root depth, Esc-from-input closes the palette and Esc-from-menu refocuses input. ''Shift-Esc'' is the universal "I'm done" — closes from any focus and any depth in one keystroke. ''Type-ahead'': pressing any printable character (no Ctrl/Alt/Meta) while focus is on a pill strip, the menu, the detail drawer or the preview background — and no section gesture claimed it — refocuses the input and appends the character, so you can start filtering from anywhere without first Tabbing back.

! Hotkey

|!Key |!Section |!Action |
|''Ctrl-Space'' |any |Open the palette |
|''Tab'' |any |Cycle focus within the current group only: pills (preset → visibility → filter → view → structure → leader) or main (input → menu → details). Rows only join the cycle when active. |
|''Shift-Tab'' |any |Jump between the two groups, restoring the focus you last held in the target group. Falls back to the bottom-most active pill (entering pills) / input (returning to main) when that slot is gone or unvisited. |
|''Enter'' |input / menu / details |Fire the selected item and close the palette. ''Exception:'' in input focus, if the current text matches a known filter or visibility prefix with a non-empty argument, Enter commits that pill instead. |
|''Ctrl-Enter'' |any |Fire the selected item but keep the palette open. Shift-Enter is a silent alias for back-compat (removed in v0.3). |
|''Alt-Enter'' |input / menu / details |Fire the selected row's ''primary row-icon'' (e.g. the 🌐 glyph opens an external URL in a new tab). No-op when the row has no icons resolved. |
|''Ctrl-Alt-Enter'' |input / menu / details |Fire the row's primary icon's ''secondary'' action — e.g. the 🌐 glyph copies the URL to the clipboard. No-op when the icon declares no `ca-row-icon-alt-*` gesture. |
|''Ctrl-DEL / Ctrl-Backspace'' |any |Clear ''both'' constraint strips (filters + visibility) AND the active-preset marker in one step. |
|''Esc'' |input |Pop one stage (back). At root depth (nothing to pop), closes the palette. |
|''Shift-Esc'' |any |Close the palette directly from any focus and any depth, in one keystroke. |
|''↓'' |input |Step into the menu (only if results exist) |
|''↑'' |input |Enter the pill group at the bottom-most active pill row (no-op if no pills active) |
|''(typing)'' |input |Filter the current stage. When the text matches a filter prefix, the input picks up a blue underline ("↵ commit filter: …"); when it matches a visibility prefix, an orange underline ("↵ commit visibility: …"); when it matches a leader key, an amber underline — leader fires after 500ms idle, any keystroke cancels. |
|''Esc'' |any (in pick-mode) |Cancel pick-mode — return to prior view without committing a filter |
|''Esc'' |preset / visibility / filter / view / details |Return focus to the input (without closing) |
|''Esc'' |menu |Pop one stage (back). At root depth, refocuses input (since there's nothing to pop). Symmetric with ArrowLeft-in-menu. |
|''← / →'' |visibility / filter |Move focus between pills within the row (clamps at edges) |
|''← / →'' |view / preset |Move focus between pills ''and apply on landing'' — these are single-select strips, so navigating IS selecting (no Space/Enter needed; clamps at edges). On preset the trailing ''+'' save pill is skipped — it stays an explicit Enter/Space gesture. (Lens choosers now live in the Structure strip's view→channel tree and cycle on ↵/Space, not on ←/→ landing.) |
|''Enter / Space'' |lens slot |Apply the focused lens (←/→ also applies on landing). On the ''➕ New…'' pill: start authoring a new lens for this slot (filter editor with a live match-count → name → save). |
|''e'' |lens slot (focused lens) |Edit the focused lens — reopens its projection filter live (a user lens is overwritten in place; a shipped lens is saved as a new copy). |
|''DEL / Backspace'' |lens slot (focused lens) |Delete the focused lens via a confirm drill (shipped lenses refuse — press ''e'' to clone instead). To turn a slot ''off'' instead, ← to its ''(off)'' / ''(default)'' head pill. |
|''DEL / Backspace'' |view |Delete the focused view via a confirm drill (shipped views refuse — fork via ''Manage views'' instead). ''Manage views → Fork current view'' makes a fully independent persisted copy: the `ca-view-*` fields PLUS a private copy of every explicit channel and grouping axis the view references (titles rewritten), so editing the fork's structure never touches the original. The built-in entries channel is referenced, not copied. |

!! Editing a view's long-tail fields

The Structure strip edits a view's ''core structure'' (roots / children / leaf / label / axis chain) and enum facets (sort / include-entries / grouping) live, with preview. Everything else — the ''long tail'' — is edited from ''Manage views → Edit all fields…'', a drill that lists every remaining view-scoped field as an editable row, grouped:

* ''identity'' — `ca-view-name`, `ca-view-hint`, `ca-icon`, `ca-order`
* ''display'' — `ca-view-count-format` (text); `ca-view-show-count`, `ca-view-containers-first`, `ca-view-show-action-preview`, `ca-view-show-side-preview`, `ca-view-context-aware` (yes/no toggles)
* ''sort detail'' — `ca-view-sort-field`, `ca-view-sort-key`
* ''picking'' — `ca-view-pick-mode`, `ca-view-pick-emits-filter`, `ca-view-after-fire`
* ''row defaults'' — `ca-view-row-hint`, `ca-view-row-icon`, `ca-view-row-order`, `ca-view-row-next-scope`, `ca-view-row-items-from` (the per-row overrides not surfaced as Structure-strip pills)
* ''preview'' — `ca-view-preview`, `ca-view-preview-name`, `ca-view-preview-title` (the view-level Overview-row summary)
* ''channels'' — each explicit channel the view composes drills into its OWN field editor (name, `ca-channel-source`, `ca-channel-include-position`, the `ca-channel-row-*` defaults, and a ''preview'' group: `ca-channel-preview`, `ca-channel-preview-name`, `ca-channel-preview-title`)

User views edit in place; a ''shipped'' (shadow-only) view or channel is read-only here and offers fork-to-edit (view) or a Structure-strip hint (channel) instead — editing in place would write an override. `ca-position-<view-slug>` is NOT edited here: per-entry placement lives on each ''entry'' tiddler, not the view.

!! Editing entries & actions in-palette

''Manage entries'' and ''Manage actions'' (top-level menu) list every command entry / action with a ''+ New …'' creator and one drillable row each. Drilling a row opens its field editor (`cp-entry-edit-rows` / `cp-action-edit-rows`):

* ''Entry'' — identity (`ca-name`/`ca-icon`/`ca-hint`/`ca-order`), `ca-kind` (leaf | drill), leaf behaviour (`ca-actions`, `ca-after-fire`, `ca-confirm` + `ca-confirm-consequence`), and drill target (`ca-next-scope`, `ca-items-from`, `ca-next-title`, `ca-next-entity-type`). Per-view placement (`ca-position-<view-slug>`) is set by hand on the entry (it varies per view) — a note row points this out.
* ''Action'' — identity, the three discovery facets (`ca-entity-type` = catalogue match · `ca-applies` = filter match · `ca-action-when` = narrowing — see [[Dev Workflow|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/dev-workflow]] §"Debugging action discovery"), and behaviour (`ca-actions`, `ca-after-fire`, `ca-confirm` + consequence).

Creating prompts for a name then saves a fresh definition under the plugin namespace with sane defaults (entry: `ca-kind: leaf`; action: empty `ca-applies`), reopening the list with the new row under ''Your …''. USER definitions edit in place; a ''shipped'' (shadow-only) one is clone-protected — ''📋 Clone to a custom … to edit'' copies it first (an in-place edit would write a shadow-masking override). Delete is confirm-gated (user definitions only).
|''↑ / ↓'' |preset / visibility / filter / view / leader |Walk between pill rows. ↓ at the bottom-most row drops into input; ↑ at the top-most row no-ops. |
|''Enter / Space'' |view |Activate the highlighted view — pops the stack to root, rebuilds the menu. (←/→ already applies on landing, so this is mostly redundant on the view strip.) |
|''Enter / Space'' |preset |Apply the focused preset (replaces filters + visibility, switches view, keeps palette open). The applied preset becomes the ''active'' preset until cleared. (←/→ also applies on landing; only the ''+'' pill still requires Enter/Space.) On the trailing ''+'' pill: open the save-as prompt to capture current state as a new preset (same as the `s` leader). |
|''Ctrl-Enter'' |preset |Overwrite the focused preset with the current state. Only effective when the focused pill IS the active preset AND it's dirty (current state diverges from the captured baseline). No-op on the ''+'' pill. |
|''DEL / Backspace'' |preset |Push a confirm-drill to permanently delete the focused preset tiddler. Confirm with Enter, cancel with Esc. No-op on the ''+'' pill. |
|''Home / End'' |preset |Jump focus to the first preset / to the ''+'' save pill (last position) |
|''DEL / Backspace'' |filter / visibility |Remove the focused pill |
|''Enter'' |filter / visibility |Move focus into the detail pane to scroll through the full help text |

|''↑ / ↓'' |structure (compact) |Walk to adjacent pill section (up = previous, down = next or input) |
|''← / →'' |structure (expanded) |Move focus between pills within the current sub-row |

|''Esc'' |structure (expanded) |Collapse back to compact view (focus stays on strip) |

|''Space'' on toggle |menu |Flip the bound value (palette stays open) |
|''Space'' on text/number/date |menu |Enter edit mode — bound value pushed into input, Enter commits, Esc cancels |
|''Space'' on any tiddler row |menu |If no kind-specific Space handler applies, scans applicable actions for the row's tiddler. Two paths run in parallel: catalogue (action `ca-entity-type` matches the row's bound type) and filter (action `ca-applies` filter non-empty with `<currentTiddler>` = row title). Union of matches opens the action-menu stage. Empty match → silent no-op. Works in catalogue and tree views, leaf and container rows. |
|''+ / -'' on number |menu |Adjust by `ca-step` (default 1). Shift = `ca-step-medium` (5). Ctrl = `ca-step-large` (20). Matched on physical key (Equal/NumpadAdd/Minus/NumpadSubtract) so layout is irrelevant. |
|''DEL / Backspace'' |menu |On an overridden setting → confirm drill to restore default. On a non-shadow tiddler in a diagnostic list → confirm drill to delete. On a synthetic row declaring `ca-on-delete` → fires that action (confirm-wrapped iff `ca-on-delete-consequence` is set). Otherwise no-op. |
|''Shift-DEL / Shift-Backspace'' |menu (root stage) |Add a ''hide-entry'' visibility pill for the selected row — the entry disappears from the root menu until the pill is removed. |
|''Ctrl-↑ / Ctrl-↓'' |menu |On a synthetic row declaring `ca-on-move-up` / `ca-on-move-down` → fires that action (typically swaps the row with its neighbour in the parent tiddler's JSON array). `stage.selectedIndex` is pre-bumped so selection follows the row. No action declared → falls through to bare ↑/↓ (selection nudge). |
|''← / →'' |details |Switch template tab when multiple templates apply |
|''↑ / ↓'' |details |Scroll the drawer natively |
|''Hold Ctrl'' |any |Open the detail drawer; release to hide. Always-on mode keeps it visible. Suppressed in edit mode. |
|''← / →'' |preview |Cycle between candidate previews when two or more apply — applies on landing (selecting IS navigating; no Enter/Space). No-op with a single candidate. |
|''Esc'' |preview |Return focus to the input. The pane stays visible — it's stack-attached, not focus-attached. |
|''↑ / ↓'' |preview |Native scroll inside the pane. |
|''Click'' on a result row |menu |Sets focus → selects → fires (Shift-click = keep open) |
|''Click'' on a filter / visibility pill |filter / visibility |Focus that pill (the × on the pill removes it) |
|''Click'' on a view pill |view |Activate that view |
|''Click'' on a preset pill |preset |Apply that preset |
|''Click'' on a leader pill |leader |Fire that leader (same as Enter / typed-gesture commit) |
|''Click'' on a breadcrumb segment | |Pop back to that stage |
|''Hover'' on any row | |Native browser tooltip shows the row's `ca-hint` text. |
|''Hover'' on a pill |filter / visibility / preset |Native browser tooltip shows the pill's hint. |

The hotkey is configured at `$:/config/shortcuts/rimir-cascade-palette-open`.

! Shipped views (concrete shapes)

The built-in views compose channels as follows:

|!View |!Channels |!Notes |
|`entries` |implicit single channel (`roots: [tag[…/entry]]`); built-in entries channel not appended (auto, flat) |Default view; surfaces all plugin-declared entry tiddlers |
|`all-tiddlers` |implicit single channel (`roots: [!is[system]]`); built-in entries channel not appended (auto, flat) |Flat list of user tiddlers; row-actions navigate |
|`by-namespace` |implicit single channel (`roots: [!is[system]cp-child-of[]]`, `children: [!is[system]cp-child-of<currentTiddler>]`); built-in entries channel auto-appended |Path-segment tree via the plugin's `cp-child-of` filter operator |
|`by-parent` |implicit single channel (`roots: [tag[TableOfContents]]`, `children: [tag<currentTiddler>]`); built-in entries channel auto-appended |TW tag-tree |
|`by-namespace-pick` |same as `by-namespace` plus `ca-view-pick-mode: yes` |Hidden pick variant — Enter commits picked tiddler as filter arg |
|`hybrid` |two explicit channels (`channels/tag-tree` + `channels/path-tree`) plus built-in entries channel |Demo view exercising multi-channel composition. Rows from each channel interleave by sort; the channel name becomes the default `ca-group` per row |
|`by-date` |implicit single channel (`roots: [!is[system]!is[shadow]]`); chain `[by-year-created, by-month-created, by-day-created]` |Demo view exercising the axis chain. Pure grouping — no `children`, so day buckets contain tiddler leaves directly. |

The `cp-child-of` filter operator is shipped by this plugin (`widgets/cp-filter-ops.js`). Its operand is the parent tiddler title; with an empty operand it returns titles that contain no `/`. Authors writing custom path-style views can reuse it directly.

! Filter operators

The plugin ships four filter operators authors can reuse from any wikitext. All are pure, side-effect-free, and self-emit their source feed (no upstream `source` required unless noted).

|!Operator |!Operand |!Source |!Emits |
|`cp-child-of[<parent>]` |Parent tiddler title (empty → root level) |Ignored |Direct path-segment children of `<parent>` (titles whose prefix is `<parent>/` and whose remainder contains no further `/`). With an empty operand, titles that have no `/` at all. |
|`cp-actions-for[<entity-type>]` |Entity-type name (empty / `*` → globals only) |Ignored |Action titles (`$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action`, drafts excluded) whose `ca-entity-type` matches the operand OR is `*`. Mirrors the catalogue + globals branches of `loadActionsForType`. |
|`cp-actions-applying-to[<title>]` |Target tiddler title (empty → no results) |Ignored |Action titles whose `ca-applies` filter returns non-empty with `currentTiddler` bound to the operand. Skips actions without `ca-applies` and actions whose `ca-applies` is blank. Mirrors `actionAppliesViaFilter`. |
|`cp-position-of[<view-slug>]` |View slug (empty → resolves base `ca-position` only) |Per-title input feed |For each input entry title, emits its effective tree-position parents in the named view. Resolution chain: `ca-position-<slug>` → `ca-position` → `at-root`. A blank slug field falls back to `ca-position`; `"none"` excludes the entry from that view. Multi-value via colon / newline split. |

These operators are reusable from any wikitext — kind-style "N actions" badges, namespace navigators, view diagnostics, etc.

! Macros

`$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/macros` (tagged `$:/tags/Macro`, imported by the palette's startup `\import` pragma) ships author-friendly wrappers:

|!Macro |!Equivalent filter |
|`cp.label(node)` |`[<node>get[caption]!is[blank]] :else[<node>get[ca-name]!is[blank]] :else[<node>]` — standard label fallback chain |
|`cp.actions-applying-to(title)` |`[cp-actions-applying-to<title>]` — friendlier alias |

A behavioural note for `by-namespace`: tree nodes are tiddlers, not derived path segments. If `foo/bar/baz` exists but no tiddler `foo` or `foo/bar` is present, those intermediate segments do not appear as drillable folders — create real tiddlers (even with empty body) at the parent paths to make them navigable.

! Entity-type drill on tree-view rows

The action menu for a typed row is reachable via two keys:

* ''Right-arrow'' on a ''leaf'' with a non-empty entity type — same gesture as the drill-into-instance flow inside `ca-next-scope` stages.
* ''Space'' on ''any'' typed row (leaf ''or'' container) — generalised action trigger. On containers, Right-arrow keeps its "descend into children" semantic, so Space is the only key that opens actions for a folder-style node.

Space also keeps its existing per-kind bindings (toggle / text / number / date edit) — those win when the row matches one of those kinds. Entity-type firing only applies when no kind-specific Space handler claims the keystroke.

The entity type is computed per row by the row's emitting channel:

* `ca-channel-row-entity-type` filter on a channel tiddler, OR
* `ca-view-row-entity-type` filter on an implicit-channel view

Both are evaluated with `<currentTiddler>` bound to the row's title. A non-empty first result is the entity type. Actions tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action` with `ca-entity-type` matching that type (or `*` for global) populate the action menu.

!! Filter-based action applicability

An action may further gate itself per entity instance by declaring `ca-action-when` — a filter evaluated with `<currentTiddler>` bound to the picked entity. A non-empty result means the action is applicable; empty / missing filter means always applicable (the default, back-compat with pre-0.0.39 actions).

Typical patterns:
* `[<currentTiddler>!has[done]]` — "Mark done" only shows for tiddlers without a `done` field
* `[<currentTiddler>!is[system]]` — "Delete" only on user tiddlers
* `[<currentTiddler>tags[]match[project]]` — domain-specific action only on tagged tiddlers

The applicability filter runs both when the action menu opens (deciding which actions to show) and when the per-row action-preview badge is computed (counting applicable actions for each visible typed row).

!! Per-row action preview

When a tree-view row carries a resolved entity type, the renderer shows a small `→N` badge next to the row name, where `N` is the count of actions that would appear if the user pressed Space on the row (or Right-arrow on a leaf). The count is computed by running the action loader (entity-type match + `ca-action-when` evaluation) for each visible row, including containers (which can't be reached via Right-arrow since that descends — Space is the action trigger on those).

The count is memoized by `(entity-type, row-title)` within a single render pass — keystroke-driven recomputations that just narrow the visible result list hit the cache. Per-view opt-out: set `ca-view-show-action-preview: no`. Stage / wiki changes invalidate the cache.

!! Perf footer (diagnostic)

When `$:/config/rimir/cascade-palette/show-perf-footer` is `yes`, a small footer renders below the hint row with the latest:

* `recompute` — milliseconds for `recomputeStage` (filter evaluation + sort)
* `render` — milliseconds for `renderStage` (DOM construction)
* `items / results` — pre/post query-filter row counts
* `actions Xms (N rows)` — total action-preview evaluation time + how many rows were preview-evaluated (only shown when non-zero)

Use it to spot slow filters (large `recompute`), expensive views with many rows, or to gauge the cost of per-row action preview before disabling it on a view.

The plugin ships five axes for the common cases. All live under `$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/axes/`.

|!Axis |!Key |!Sort |!Notes |
|`by-year-created` |`[get[created]format:date[YYYY]]` |`desc` |Newest year first. Pair with month + day for journaling-style trees. |
|`by-month-created` |`[get[created]format:date[MMM]]` |`enum` |Jan…Dec via `ca-axis-sort-keys`. |

Page-session-only (stored under `$:/temp/`, clears on reload). Iterate via `[enlist<sticky-context-list>]`. Empty string when nothing is pinned — context-aware filters then naturally produce no narrowing. Mutated by the universal Pin / Unpin / Clear verbs, the ''`+<title>`'' input prefix, and any row action that sends `rimir-cascade-palette-pin-context` / `-unpin-context` / `-clear-context`. |
|`<<sticky-context-count>>` |entries, actions, filters, visibility |Count of pinned tiddlers as a string (''"0"'', ''"1"'', …). For badge text and conditional UI inside templates. |
|`<arg>` |filter / visibility tiddler `expr` field |The sanitised user-supplied argument. Operand-form: `[<arg>]`. |
|`<<arg>>` |filter / visibility tiddler `chip` / `hint` / `help` fields |Plain-text version of the same argument. |

! Mount point

The widget is injected into `document.body` at boot via the startup module `widgets/cascade-palette-startup.js`. Mount-point ID: `rimir-cascade-palette-mount`. To inspect: `document.getElementById("rimir-cascade-palette-mount")`.

! Console diagnostics

The widget only logs on error paths (no boot noise):

* `[cascade-palette] startup mount complete — widget in document.body` — startup module ran successfully (one-time at boot)
* `[cascade-palette] action invocation failed: ...` — `invokeViaNavigator()` threw (most likely a filter or wikitext error in `ca-actions` / `ca-next-scope` / `ca-next-default-action`)
* `[cascade-palette] ca-visibility-filter error on ...` — a root-entry's visibility filter threw; entry stays visible defensively
* `[cascade-palette] ca-template-applies error on ...` — a template's filter threw; template is excluded
* `[cascade-palette] template render error ...` — the template body wikitext failed to parse; the drawer shows the error message in place of the template
* `[cascade-palette] stack depth N exceeds soft warning M — possible cascade loop?` — the user has drilled past the soft-depth-warning threshold
* `[cascade-palette] view root set N rows exceeds threshold M — …` — the active view resolves more rows than the large-root-set-warning threshold (rebuilt + decorated every keystroke); fired once per view, re-armed when the set drops back below

<$fill $name="body">

This page documents the TiddlyWiki-specific machinery cascade-palette uses (and the traps it dodges). Most of it lives in `widgets/cascade-palette-widget.js` and a handful of subsystem libraries. Read this when you're about to touch the engine source — not when authoring declarative content.

! Startup mounting (`cascade-palette-startup.js`)

The palette widget mounts at boot via a startup module — NOT via a page-template tag. This makes the palette work uniformly in any UI mode (default wiki, appify-replaced story river, custom themes).

* ''`exports.after = ["render"]`'' — runs after the page widget tree is built (so `$tw.pageWidgetNode` exists).
* The startup imports `\import [all[shadows+tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/Macro]!has[draft.of]]` so `$:/tags/Macro`-tagged `\function` defs (including the plugin's own `macros.tid`) are visible to every filter and action wikitext evaluated by the widget.
* The widget mounts via `<$cascade-palette/>` into `document.body`, OUTSIDE the page widget tree. This has one consequence — see ''Navigator routing'' below.

The widget is mostly idle until `Ctrl-Space` (or the configured hotkey) is pressed. The hotkey is bound via a standard TW keyboard-shortcut tiddler (`config/shortcut-binding.tid`) and sends a `rimir-cascade-palette-open` message that the widget catches via `$tw.rootWidget`.

! Navigator routing (`cp-actions.js:findActionParent` / `invokeViaNavigator`)

Because the widget mounts in `document.body`, action widgets it invokes via `$tw.wiki.invokeActions` would by default see only `$tw.rootWidget` as their parent. That means navigator-routed messages (''`$action-navigate`'', `tm-edit-tiddler`, `tm-close-tiddler`, …) would have no `<$navigator>` ancestor to dispatch to — and silently drop.

The widget's `findActionParent()` walks `$tw.pageWidgetNode`'s subtree looking for:

# A ''statewrap widget'' (deepest one) — preferred when present, because `getStatewrapContext` (rimir/statewrap) walks the parent chain UP and needs to see `statewrap.statewrapContext`. Statewrap sits INSIDE appify-app, so picking it gives both statewrap context AND any ancestor navigators (events bubble UP).
# Otherwise the first ''navigator widget''.
# Otherwise `$tw.rootWidget` (root-level handlers like `tm-save-wiki` still work).

`invokeViaNavigator(actionString, variables)` parses the action wikitext with `parentWidget: parent`, makes the widget tree with the same parent, renders into `$tw.fakeDocument`, and calls `invokeActions`. The action then dispatches into the page-tree-aware parent and bubbles correctly.

! The `makeFakeWidget` invariant

Every place the engine evaluates a filter (`wiki.filterTiddlers`) MUST pass a widget that has `makeFakeWidgetWithVariables` on it. TW's run-prefixes (`:filter`, `:map`, `:reduce`, `:sortsub`) call back into that method to spawn per-iteration child widgets — a plain object stub throws `TypeError: widget.makeFakeWidgetWithVariables is not a function` and silently drops the prefix's whole result.

The widget centralises this through ''`proto.makeFakeWidget(variables)`'' (`cp-actions.js:197`):

```js
proto.makeFakeWidget = function (variables) {
    // Delegates to TW core's Widget.prototype.makeFakeWidgetWithVariables —
    // it channels `variables` on top of this widget's parent chain (so both
    // injected literals AND $:/tags/Macro-tagged \function defs imported by
    // the startup \import resolve correctly), AND propagates
    // makeFakeWidgetWithVariables onto the returned fake widget so nested
    // prefixes work.
    return this.makeFakeWidgetWithVariables(variables);
};
```

Rule for new code: every `wiki.filterTiddlers(filter, ?)` callsite that injects variables routes through `this.makeFakeWidget(vars)`. Never construct a `{getVariable, wiki}` stub by hand. See [[tw-gotchas-widget-context#Custom fake widgets passed to wiki.filterTiddlers…]] in the project-wide gotchas memory.

! Stage stack & persistence (`cp-stack.js`)

The palette is a stack of stages (`this.stack`), each a small POJO:

|!Field |!Meaning |
|`kind` |`"root"` / `"tree"` / `"filter"` / `"actions"` / `"confirm"` |
|`query` |Current text typed at this stage |
|`items` / `results` |Pre-filter and post-query rows |
|`selectedIndex` |Which row is highlighted |
|`parentPath` |For tree-stages: array of bucket keys (axes) + tiddler titles (recursive) |
|`_previewContext` / `_previewActiveTemplate` |For side-preview pinning |
|`_freezeItems` |Used by the axis picker (a sub-stage with frozen item list) |

''Session persistence.'' `close()` paths split: ''preserve'' (Shift-Esc, action-fire close) writes `JSON.stringify(safe)` to `$:/temp/rimir/cascade-palette/saved-stack`; ''reset'' (plain Esc at root, backdrop click) clears it. `openPalette()` reads on each open; if present, restores (`items`/`results` left empty for `recomputeStage` to repopulate). `confirm` and `actions` stages are dropped on serialise — they reference closure-captured strings — so the saved chain truncates at the first such stage.

''Compact JSON only.'' Writes are `JSON.stringify(root)` with no indent, no newlines. This avoids [[tw-gotchas-filesystem-sync#Non-text field with newline / control chars silently switches `.tid` → `.json` file format]] — TW's filesystem adapter flips a tiddler from `.tid` to `.json` if any non-`text` field contains `\n` / `\t` / leading-whitespace.

! Filter substitution (`cp-actions.js:buildStageVariables`)

The widget exposes variables to every filter and action wikitext via a synthetic widget context:

|!Variable |!What it is |
|`<<query>>` |Current input text |
|`<<picked>>` |For action invocation: the title just picked (the entity the action acts on) |
|`<<parent-picked>>` |Title picked in the parent stage (one back) |
|`<<stage-N-picked>>` |Title picked at stage index N (root = 0) |
|`<<context-tiddler>>` |Tiddler the user was looking at when the hotkey fired (focused [data-tiddler-title] ancestor, falling back to $:/HistoryList) |
|`<<stage-preview-context>>` |Inside a preview-bearing subtree: the entity the side preview is pinned to |
|`<<currentTiddler>>` |Per-row binding when relevant (axis evaluation, row-actions, applies-filters) |

`buildStageVariables(stage, picked, extras)` is the canonical builder. New callsites that inject extras should pass them via the `extras` map instead of hand-constructing a separate variables object — keeps the surface uniform and audit-able.

! Side-preview pane (`cp-side-preview.js`)

''Cache.'' Rendered widget trees are keyed by `(depth, contextTitle, templateTitle)`. Selection-tracking re-renders inside the same preview reuse the DOM; switching pills re-renders (template change); per-row context change re-renders.

''Reactive updates.'' The plugin's wiki change hook (`cascade-palette-widget.js`) dispatches `refresh(changes)` into the cached widget tree for non-invalidating changes — form inputs inside a preview template stay reactive without rebuild — and drops the cache entirely when the active template tiddler, the context tiddler, or any side-preview-tagged tiddler is created/modified/deleted.

''Activation paths.'' `_attachPreviewToStage` recognises (a) per-menu template set; (b) tag-only opt-in (row sets `ca-preview-context` / `ca-preview-per-row` without a template — pane activates from tag candidates only); (c) inheritance from a parent per-row stage.

! Axis-key memoisation (`cp-axes.js`)

Axis `keyFn` results are memoised per `(axisTitle + paramsHash) × tiddlerTitle`, invalidated on `wiki.getChangeCount()`. First touch of the cache fills it; subsequent re-renders cost O(rows visited at the current depth), not O(source).

The `groupBy` / `sortGroups` primitive is loaded from `$:/plugins/rimir/mindmap/lib/grouped-tree.js` when the mindmap plugin is installed (soft-dep); a tiny inline fallback covers the case where mindmap isn't around — same algorithm, no feature degradation.

! Prototype-extension contract

`cascade-palette-widget.js` constructs the prototype, then 21 `cp-*.js` library modules `require()` and patch methods onto it. The require order does NOT matter — patches are static (every method is installed before any method is called) — but modules read each other's state and methods at runtime:

* ''Shared instance fields'' on `this` (initialised in the constructor) form the de-facto contract between modules. The constructor lists them in five logical groups (lifecycle / focus / constraints / view-preset-leader / transient). Touch with care; renaming a field requires grep across modules.
* ''Cross-module method calls'' are not explicitly typed. cp-filters / cp-visibility / cp-reach-pills / cp-field-pills / cp-preset-pills / cp-leaders all call `this.recomputeStage` (cp-stack) and `this._flashElement` (cp-leaders). cp-pick-presets / cp-firing / cp-keyboard call `this.invokeViaNavigator` (cp-actions). The right reading direction is: every `proto.foo` is callable from anywhere; coupling lives in WHICH methods are called WHEN.

''When you add a new field to `this`,'' put it in the right logical group in the constructor with a comment explaining lifecycle (created when? cleared when? read by whom?). Future grep across `cp-*.js` is the only protection against accidental shadowing.

''When you add a new `proto.foo` method,'' if it's an internal helper, prefix with `_`. The convention is applied consistently across modules.

! Hot paths

|!Surface |!Per keystroke |!Notes |
|`recomputeStage` |1× | full filter eval + matcher + render |
|`evaluateFilterStage` |1× | `wiki.filterTiddlers` against `ca-next-scope` / view-specific source |
|`applyQueryToStage` |1× | O(items × tokens) matcher — fine for stages with ≤200 items |
|`_loadFilterTiddlers` / `_loadVisibilityTiddlers` |2–4× (cached per `wiki.getChangeCount()` from v0.0.80) | reloads invalidate only on writes |
|Deep-search BFS |opt-in via reach pills | bounded by `max-depth=4`, `max-nodes=800`, `max-ms=80` configs |

! See also

* [[Architecture|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/architecture]] — high-level component map
* [[Protocol|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol]] — declarative authoring surface
* [[Dev Workflow|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/dev-workflow]] — how to contribute & test

! Contribution tags

|!Tag suffix |!What you contribute |
|`/entry` |A root-level row — drill / fire / open |
|`/action` |An action menu item — appears when its `ca-entity-type` matches |
|`/leader` |A keyboard shortcut after `Ctrl-Space` |
|`/filter` |A Filter strip pill |
|`/visibility` |A Visibility strip pill |
|`/reach` |A Reach strip pill |
|`/field` |A Search-in strip pill |
|`/view` |An alternate view of the same data |
|`/channel` |A reusable channel (roots / children / decorations) referenced by views via `ca-view-channels` |
|`/axis` |A reusable grouping axis (derive-key spec) referenced by channels via `ca-channel-axes` |
|`/preset` |A pre-shipped configuration snapshot |
|`/template` |A row-detail-drawer template (Ctrl-hold) |
|`/help` |A help section (you're reading the output) |
|`/diagnostic` |A diagnostic tile shown under Configurations → Diagnostics |
|`/setting` |A settings row shown under Configurations → Settings |

Each tag prefix is `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette` — e.g. the full tag for a help section is `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help`.

! Help section schema (this surface)

|!Field |!Purpose |
|`ca-name` |Display name |
|`ca-icon` |Glyph |
|`ca-group` |Category for visual grouping. Use `Plugin: <slug>` to land in the Plugins drill. |
|`ca-order` |Sort order (lower first) |
|`ca-hint` |One-line subtitle |
|`text` |Wikitext body rendered in the side preview |

! Where to put your tiddler

* ''In a plugin'' — `$:/plugins/<author>/<plugin>/help/<slug>`. One tiddler per plugin is the convention.
* ''In a wiki'' — any title works; just tag it `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help`.

''→'' Every field of every protocol: <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol">doc/protocol</$link>
"},"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/axes":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/axes","tags":"$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help","ca-name":"Axes","ca-icon":"📐","ca-group":"Pills","ca-order":"250","ca-hint":"Group any tree by year, status, prefix — chain axes inside a channel.","ca-kind":"leaf","ca-actions":"<$action-navigate $to=<<picked>>/>","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"An ''axis'' is a reusable derive-key spec — a filter that maps each tiddler to a bucket key (a year, a status, the first tag, anything). A channel can chain several axes to build a grouped tree:

''year → month → day → tiddlers in that day''.

Each axis runs at one tree depth. Drilling into a bucket narrows the source set to rows whose key matches the bucket, then re-enters at the next axis.

! Where to find it

* ''Pick a grouped view:'' Tab into the view strip, switch to ''By date'' — the shipped demo (axes: year → month → day, no children).
* ''Edit any channel's chain in-place:'' Tab to the ''Structure'' strip, press Enter / → to expand. Each channel's mini-row shows its current chain as yellow ''by'' / ''→'' pills, ending in a dashed ''+''. The strip is hidden when there are no pills to show.

! Editing the chain

|!Gesture |!Effect |
|''Backspace'' / ''Delete'' on a focused axis pill |Remove that axis from the chain |
|''Shift-←'' / ''Shift-→'' on a focused axis pill |Reorder within the chain |
|''Enter'' on a focused axis pill |Open the picker in ''replace'' mode |
|''Enter'' / ''Space'' on the ''+'' pill |Open the picker in ''append'' mode |
|''Esc'' in the picker |Cancel — no change to the chain |

The picker is itself a cascade stage listing every axis registered in the wiki. On commit, the new chain is written to a session-state tiddler — survives reload, but isn't filesystem-synced. Delete that state tiddler to revert the channel to its declared default.

! Axes vs. children — one descent, two halves

|!Channel has |!Result |
|axes only |Pure grouping. Buckets all the way down; deepest buckets contain tiddler leaves. |
|children only |Today's recursive tree (''By parent'', ''By namespace''). Axes never engage. |
|axes + children |Buckets at the top, recursive tree at the bottom. E.g. "TOC tiddlers grouped by year, each TOC then expanding its tag-subtree." |
|neither |Flat list of `roots`. |

The two never fight: axes own the top of the tree, children owns the bottom. The transition happens at the depth where the chain runs out — that's the only place they meet, in the leaf-detection check (''does `children` return anything under this tiddler?'').

! Shipped axes

<$list filter="[all[shadows+tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/axis]sort[ca-axis-name]]" variable="axis">|`<$view tiddler=<<axis>> field="ca-axis-name"/>` |<$view tiddler=<<axis>> field="ca-axis-hint"/> |
</$list>

! Authoring your own

Tag a tiddler `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/axis` with at minimum a `ca-axis-name` and a `ca-axis-key` filter:

```
title: $:/plugins/example/axes/by-first-tag
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/axis
ca-axis-name: First tag
ca-axis-key: [tags[]first[]]
ca-axis-sort: asc
ca-axis-empty-label: untagged
```

The next palette open picks it up. Attach it to a channel via `ca-channel-axes` (or `ca-view-axes` on an implicit-channel view) — space-separated tiddler titles, in chain order.

''→'' Full axis schema + composition rules: <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol">doc/protocol</$link> (Axes section).

Built-in keys

|!Key |!Effect |
|`Ctrl-Space` |Open / reset palette |
|`Tab` |Cycle focus section (within current group) |
|`Shift-Tab` |Jump between pill-group (top strips) and main group (input/menu/details/preview) |
|`↑` `↓` |Move row selection |
|`→` |Drill — descend tree containers, push action menu on typed catalogue rows |
|`←` |Pop one stage |
|`← →` (in pills) |Move between pills. On the single-select strips (view / preset) landing on a pill ''applies it'' — no Space/Enter needed (preset's ''+'' excepted). Lens choosers moved into the Structure strip's view→channel tree (↵/Space cycles, `l` locks). |
|`↵` |Fire selected row |
|`Ctrl-↵` |Fire + keep palette open |
|`Alt-↵` |Fire row's primary icon (e.g. 🌐 opens URL in new tab) |
|`Ctrl-Alt-↵` |Fire row icon's secondary action (e.g. 🌐 copies URL) |
|`Space` |Open action menu on any row whose tiddler has applicable actions (works in tree views via `ca-applies` filter); also: toggle / edit kind-specific rows |
|any character |Type-ahead: a printable key pressed in any non-input section that no section gesture claimed jumps focus to the input and appends the character — start typing from anywhere to filter |
|`Esc` |Pop stage; from root, close |
|`Shift-Esc` |Close palette outright |
|`DEL` |Remove focused pill / reset row to default |
|`Ctrl-DEL` |Clear all pills in focused strip |
|`Ctrl-↑` `Ctrl-↓` |Reorder row (when row declares move actions) |
|hold `Ctrl` |Show row detail drawer |

! Leaders (registered live)

The cascade keeps the input focused while you type a leader key — once you stop typing (idle window, default 500ms), the leader fires. Plugins can register new leaders; the table below reflects what's currently in the wiki.

|!Key |!Name |!Description |
<$list filter="[all[shadows+tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/leader]sort[ca-leader-key]]" variable="leader">|`<$view tiddler=<<leader>> field="ca-leader-key"/>` |<$view tiddler=<<leader>> field="ca-leader-name"><$view tiddler=<<leader>> field="title"/></$view> |<$view tiddler=<<leader>> field="ca-leader-hint"/> |
</$list>

''→'' Full key reference: <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/reference">doc/reference</$link>
"},"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/pills":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/pills","tags":"$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help","ca-name":"Pills","ca-icon":"💊","ca-group":"Pills","ca-order":"200","ca-hint":"Six independent pill strips compose the palette's state.","ca-kind":"leaf","ca-actions":"<$action-navigate $to=<<picked>>/>","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Pills are the palette's persistent state. Each strip is a separate concern, sits in its own row, and uses the same push / DEL / Tab-cycle grammar.

! The six strips

|!Strip |!Concern |!Activation |!Mutual exclusion |
|''Preset'' |Snapshot every other strip's state and recall it as one |Leaders `s` (save) and `r` (recall) |No — one preset can be "active" but stacking presets is meaningless |
|''Filter'' |Narrow which rows the engine considers |Leader `>` (push by title) or `+` picker pill |No |
|''Visibility'' |Hide whole entry groups via filter |`v` leaders set by tiddlers tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/visibility` |No |
|''View'' |Switch between alternate trees of the same data |Leader (one per view) |Yes — exactly one view active |
|''Reach'' |Where to search (here vs. whole tree) |Leaders `d` (Here) and `g` (Everywhere) |Yes — pushing one evicts the other |
|''Search-in'' |Which fields the matcher reads |Leader `a` (all) or individual leaders per field |No — pills accumulate (union semantics) |

! Plus: the Structure strip

Below the view strip sits a ''Structure'' strip (only visible when the active view declares channels). Tab into it, Enter / → to expand into the view→channel tree: a ''view'' header row leading with three lens choosers (Name / Icon / Note — the view's default row decorations; ''`l`'' toggles a lock) and one indented ''channel'' mini-row each. A channel's mini-row leads with its own three lens choosers (overriding or inheriting the view default), then its primitive pills (roots / children / leaf / label / row decorations) AND its ''axis chain'' as yellow ''by'' / ''→'' pills + a dashed ''+'' pill to append. Lens choosers cycle on ↵/Space, the axis chain edits live (Backspace removes, Shift-←/→ reorders, Enter swaps); the remaining primitive pills are read-only here (edit them via ''Manage views → Edit all fields…''). The view header and each explicit channel mini-row also carry a ''summary'' pill — the Overview-row template (`ca-view-preview` / `ca-channel-preview`): ↵ edits it, DEL clears it, ''—'' shows when unset.

See <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/axes">Axes</$link> for the axis grammar and edit gestures.

! Common grammar

* Pills appear as text chips with an `×` close button.
* `Tab` cycles focus into a strip; `←` / `→` move along the strip.
* `DEL` on a focused pill removes it.
* `Ctrl-DEL` clears the whole strip.
* When NO pill is pushed, the strip is hidden (no visual clutter).

! Discoverability

Pills are discoverable by their leader keys (see ''Keys'' section). Leaders that push pills are tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/leader` and live in `dev-wiki/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/leaders/`.

''→'' Full pill semantics: <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol">doc/protocol</$link>
"},"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/plugins":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/plugins","tags":"$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help","ca-name":"Plugins","ca-icon":"🧩","ca-group":"Plugins","ca-order":"500","ca-kind":"drill","ca-next-scope":"[all[shadows+tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help]regexp:ca-group[^Plugin:]] +[sort[ca-order]]","ca-next-title":"Plugins","ca-hint":"Other plugins' help contributions — drill in to browse.","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Plugins that integrate with the cascade palette can each ship a single help tiddler — typically at `$:/plugins/<author>/<plugin>/help` — tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help` with `ca-group: Plugin: <slug>`. Drill into this row to browse them.

</$list>

! Why one per plugin

Plugin-contributed leaders, pills, and entries already appear automatically in the live tables under ''Keys'', ''Pills'', and ''Entries'' — the protocol tags drive those cheat-sheets. The per-plugin help tiddler exists only for narrative context: a short table summarising what the plugin adds, with a story-river link to the plugin's full docs.

! Authoring a plugin help tiddler

```
title: $:/plugins/<author>/<plugin>/help
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help
ca-name: <plugin name>
ca-icon: <glyph>
ca-group: Plugin: <slug>
ca-order: 10
ca-hint: <one-line summary>

|!Adds |!Activation |
|`<key>` leader |drills into … |
|... |... |

→ Full docs: <$link to="$:/plugins/<author>/<plugin>/doc/overview"><plugin> overview</$link>
```

"},"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/search":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/search","tags":"$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help","ca-name":"Search","ca-icon":"🔎","ca-group":"Search","ca-order":"300","ca-hint":"Reach + Meta + Field pills widen the search; three gestures pick a deep result.","ca-kind":"leaf","ca-actions":"<$action-navigate $to=<<picked>>/>","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"By default, typing in the palette filters the //current stage's// visible rows by substring match against each row's `name` and `hint` slots. Three pill strips widen this:

! Reach (where) — mutually exclusive

|!Pill |!Leader |!Walks |
|🔍 Here |`d` |Every reachable drill below the current stage |
|🌐 Everywhere |`g` |Every reachable drill from the active view's root |

Picking a Reach result replays the drill path so the cascade arrives at the row's natural parent.

! Meta (cascade-item author meta) — accumulating

Pills tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-meta`. Matcher reads `item[ca-meta-key]`.

|!Pill |!Reads |
|🏷 Name |Row's display name (default if no pills) |
|💡 Hint |Row's subtitle (default if no pills) |

! Field (literal tiddler fields) — accumulating

Pills tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/search-field`. Matcher reads `wiki.getTiddler(item.title).fields[ca-tiddler-field]`. Synthetic rows skip silently.

|!Pill |!Reads |
|📄 Text |Backing tiddler's `text` field — body |

! Push everything

Leader `a` — pushes both Meta pills (Name, Hint) plus the Text Field pill. Equivalent to "match anywhere".

Active pills in each strip //union//; the matcher reads the combined slot set.

! Multi-match visualisation

A row that matches in multiple slots gets:

* ''Inline highlight'' on its name / hint (whichever matched).
* ''One snippet line per non-displayed match'' — beneath the row, prefixed by the matched pill's chip + context window around the hit.

! Picking a deep result — three gestures

When Reach is active, results carry a drill path. Three keys distinguish what happens after the path replays:

|!Gesture |!Effect |
|`↵` Enter |Replay path + fire (drill into drills, execute leaves) |
|`→` Right |Replay path + drill only (no-op on plain leaves) |
|`Space` |''Pin only'' — replay path, select row, do NOT fire. Safe for destructive matches. |

''→'' Full deep-search docs: <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/deep-search">doc/deep-search</$link>
"},"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/sticky-context":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/sticky-context","tags":"$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help","ca-name":"Sticky context","ca-icon":"📌","ca-group":"Pills","ca-order":"210","ca-hint":"Pin tiddlers for the duration of a workday flow — call, meeting, focus.","ca-kind":"leaf","ca-actions":"<$action-navigate $to=<<picked>>/>","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"Sticky context is a list of pinned tiddler titles, persistent across cp close/reopen AND page reload. Use it to scope every view to a person you're talking to, the attendees of a meeting, or whatever entities you're focused on right now.

! Verbs

|!Verb |!How |!Effect |
|''Pin to context (any row)'' |Space on any tiddler row → "Pin to context" |Adds the row's tiddler to the sticky context strip |
|''Pin to context (typed)'' |In input: ''`+<title>`'' + Enter |Pins the typed title verbatim — no autocomplete (use Space-pin on a row for that). Indigo underline confirms the cue; bare `+` is a silent no-op |
|''Unpin from context'' |Space on a pinned row → "Unpin from context" (only shown when pinned) |Removes that tiddler from the context |
|''Clear sticky context'' |Leader ''`C`'' (capital, single keystroke + 500ms idle) |Empties the strip |

Each pin appears as a pill in the ''Context'' strip (indigo, just below the preset strip). Click `×` on a pill — or focus the strip with Tab and press `Backspace` — to remove that one pin. The strip itself is reachable via Tab/Shift-Tab/Up/Down ONLY once it has at least one pill (universal cp convention — empty strips are hidden and skipped in navigation).

! How views consume it

Two variables are bound in every filter eval routed through cp (0.0.97+):

* ''`<<sticky-context-list>>`'' — the raw title-list string (TW parseStringArray format). Feed it into `[enlist<sticky-context-list>]` to iterate.
* ''`<<sticky-context-count>>`'' — string-typed count ("0", "1", "5"…). For badge text and conditional UI.

Ambient EVERYWHERE — `ca-view-roots`, `ca-channel-children`, `ca-view-row-icon`, `ca-view-sort-key`, `ca-view-row-actions`, `:filter` predicates inside any of those, etc. You don't have to thread the variable through channel parameters.

A view ''opts in'' to context-narrowing by referencing one of these in its channel filters AND declaring ''`ca-view-context-aware: yes`'' so the view pill paints a small indigo badge when context is non-empty. The flag is just a visual cue — the actual narrowing happens in your channel's filter expression.

! Multiselect views (toggle pattern)

For a checkbox-style view (pin/unpin via Enter on each row, palette stays open), four field overrides coordinate:

* ''`ca-view-after-fire: stay`'' (view-wide keep-open default — every row fire stays open without per-row `ca-after-fire: keep`)
* ''`ca-view-row-icon: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[☑]else[☐]]`'' — checkbox glyph mirrors pin state
* ''`ca-view-sort: custom`'' + ''`ca-view-sort-key: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[0]else[1]addsuffix<currentTiddler>]`'' — pinned rows float to top
* ''`ca-view-row-actions: <$action-sendmessage $message={{{ [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[rimir-cascade-palette-unpin-context]else[rimir-cascade-palette-pin-context]] }}} title=<<currentTiddler>>/>'' — single widget; the inline-filter `$message` dispatches pin-or-unpin

The shipped ''Pick attendees'' view in `rimir/worga` is a worked example.

! Example: a "Topics for context" view

```
title: $:/plugins/.../views/topics-for-context
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view
ca-view-name: Topics for context
ca-view-context-aware: yes
ca-view-roots: [all[tiddlers]has[stakeholders]] :filter[<currentTiddler>get[stakeholders]enlist-input[] :intersection[enlist<sticky-context-list>]]
```

This emits topics whose `stakeholders` field contains at least one pinned tiddler. Without `<<sticky-context-list>>` being referenced anywhere in the channel filters, the view simply lists all topics — opt-in is real.

! Stale pins

When the target tiddler is deleted, its pill renders greyed and struck-through. The pin stays — clear it via `×` or `Backspace` when you're ready. No auto-pruning (so undo flows aren't disturbed).

! Lifetime

Stored at ''`$:/temp/rimir/cascade-palette/sticky-context`'' (field `list`). ''Page-session only'' — full reload (F5) clears it, browser-tab close clears it. Never written to disk (by TW convention for `$:/temp/`). The intent: sticky context tracks one continuous flow (a call, a meeting, an hour of focused work). If you need it to outlive a reload, capture the pinned set as a ''preset'' (`s` leader) and recall later.

! Where to put workday verbs

cp ships only the generic Pin / Unpin / Clear verbs. ''Workflow-specific'' verbs ("Take call from <currentTiddler>", "Start meeting", "End focus") and ''context-aware views'' belong in a separate plugin — see ''`rimir/worga`'' for a worked example, or build your own by tagging tiddlers `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action` / `.../leader` / `.../view`.
"},"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/welcome":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/welcome","tags":"$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/help","ca-name":"Welcome","ca-icon":"👋","ca-group":"Basics","ca-order":"100","ca-hint":"What the palette is and the four gestures that drive it.","ca-kind":"leaf","ca-actions":"<$action-navigate $to=<<picked>>/>","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"The cascade palette is a keyboard-driven command surface — a single window into actions, configuration, entities, and search that follows a small set of consistent gestures.

! Five gestures

|!Gesture |!Effect |
|`Ctrl-Space` |Open the palette anywhere. Resets to root if already open. |
|`→` |Drill — descend a tree container or push the action menu on a typed catalogue row. |
|`Space` |Open the action menu on any tiddler row with applicable actions (works in tree views too — see ''Action discovery''). |
|`Esc` |Pop the current stage. From root, closes the palette. |
|`↵` |Fire the selected row (or commit text). |

`Tab` cycles focus //between sections// (input → preset → filter → view → menu → details → …). `Shift-Tab` jumps between the pill-group (top strips) and the main group (input/menu/details/preview).

Everything else — pills, leaders, search reach, side preview, action menus — composes on top of these four.

! How sections compose

The palette has //facets// you can stack independently:

* ''Filters'' narrow the data set you're walking
* ''Reach'' widens search scope (current stage / whole tree)
* ''Search-in'' picks which fields the matcher reads
* ''Views'' switch between alternate trees of the same data
* ''Presets'' snapshot a whole configuration for one-keystroke recall

Each facet is a pill strip. Pills can be added (via leaders) and removed (DEL on a focused pill). No modal dialogs, no checkbox lists — just navigable pills.

! Where to learn more

* <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/overview">Overview</$link> — high-level architecture, the "drill is a tiddler" idea
* <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/reference">Reference</$link> — full key, field, message, config tables
* <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/protocol">Protocol</$link> — every contribution tag and the fields you can ship
* <$link to="$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/doc/examples">Examples</$link> — runnable cascade-palette fixtures
